findings.term: The centre sentence: "what a selection … reaches, what it drains beyond what it reads, how it locks on what it already chose"

examples.where: /Users/ren/tmp/wl/th2/AGENTS.md:7 (same sentence at README.md:11, README.md:177, and reshaped at ONE-PAGE.md:7)
examples.quote: It is first a map for alignment: what a selection (a reward, a judge, a market, a vote, a training run) reaches, what it drains beyond what it reads, how it locks on what it already chose.
every optimum of an order rising with what couples in drains what lies beyond as far as any eligible outcome does
where the selection is optimized to the full, it draws down whatever lies beyond from which a unit can pass into what it rewards, to the least any outcome leaves

findings.states: Three different relations, none needing a doer. (a) 'reaches': which course goes on depends only on differences along what couples in; courses alike along those couplings go on alike (同行), so a difference elsewhere makes no difference to which goes on. (b) 'drains': where a unit of a condition that does not couple in can pass into one that does, every course greatest along the coupled order has that condition at the least level any eligible course leaves. (c) 'locks … already chose': where the criterion is itself conditioned by the share that went on under it, the same share comes back step after step, and a fall in a condition that does not condition the criterion makes no difference to it.
findings.note: The sentence appears 4 times (grep); its parts recur: 'a selection' as grammatical subject 19, selection(s) 55, drain* 12, lock* 27, reach* 45, optim* 19. Five agent verbs (reaches, drains, reads, locks, chose) hang on one noun made an actor, plus a 'beyond'. Replacing any one verb keeps the shape; the sentence has to be said again as three dependences. ONE-PAGE.md:7 is already half-way ('reaches only what couples into it'). Agent nouns built the same way (selector 5, optimizer, valuer 5, shaper, drawer) are fine where they are roles in a stated relation, as ONE-PAGE.md:34 says of taker and drawn-on; ONE-PAGE.md:20 is honest that 'a selector selects through just those' is a premise. AGENTS.md's direction changes only after Ren has read it, and README.md is generated from the readme_* keys, so one re-saying serves all four places.

findings.term: The goal sentence: "a joint selection that reads beyond its own share and does not come to select for control over its own selection"; "Control of the rule is not captured"

examples.quote: an alignment that keeps humans and AI, selecting together, out of instrumental convergence and the meta-attractor: a joint selection that reads beyond its own share and does not come to select for control over its own selection
Control of the rule is not captured: where shaping the rule is selected by what comes back to the shapers
Any system can be captured by such a rule, and the theorems say exactly what holds it there

findings.states: What humans and AI together let go on stays conditioned by conditions other than the share it has favoured, and the favoured share's rise does not come to condition the criterion in that share's favour: the loop share → criterion → share does not close on the share alone. ONE-PAGE.md:30 already unpacks it as two relations: what forms the rule is conditioned by what comes back to those forming it, yet the rule stays conditioned by what is not their share, so a fall there can turn it; and a lock is left before the fall passes its point of no return.
findings.note: Sentence occurs 4 times verbatim. Control/capture phrases: 'select for control', 'control over', 'power over the rule', 'Control of the rule' 7; captur* 15; shap* 9. The sentence stacks a knower (reads), a border (beyond), a possessor (its own share, its own selection), a ruler (control over) and a container (keeps … out of). ONE-PAGE.md:30's two-part unpacking is the relational version and could carry the goal by itself.

findings.states: Two relations, one holding and one not: the course draws on a condition (or something depends on what the course changes), and that condition does not couple into the selection. 'What lies beyond what it reads' is 'what it draws on, or what depends on it, that makes no difference to it'. The difference is along coupling, not between two regions.

Four uses, only the first a finding: (1) the unread region standing free, as in README.md:17 and ONE-PAGE.md:9, where a border is presumed; (2) with its basis stated, as in README.md:120 (closure under a named relation) or 'fed from beyond' said of a listed family: fine; (3) the denials 'no should beyond becoming', 'no authority outside becoming', which use the word to deny an outside and are the author's words: keep; (4) temporal ('beyond one's death'): fine. 'within' (72) is the same container picture from the other side; fine where it denies an outside ('form within it') or is the model's term ('within what is renewed').

findings.term: reads / read (for coupling): "what it reads", "a loss it does not read", "a rule read from the share"

The selections through a selector's couplings (what it reads or needs), together, reach exactly what couples into it

findings.states: 'X reads Y' states that Y conditions X: a difference in Y makes a difference to X. 'A rule read from the share' states the reverse direction with the same word: the share conditions the rule (the page's own 'formed from the share it selects'). 'A loss it does not read' is a fall that makes no difference to the rule.
findings.note: 198 raw: about 77 are the standing word for an interpretation ('a reading', 'read as', 'read onto'), about 100 the coupling sense, plus reader(s) 15 (a person reading the text, or a member of a pool). One word does three jobs and, in the coupling sense, makes the selection a knower facing a known. It is a NAME because the pages already own the replacement ('couples into' 21, 'what couples in'), but the direction has to be chosen each time. Siblings in the same role: 'what can see its loss?' (ONE-PAGE.md:19), sense 6, observe 6, register 6, mostly with the basis stated (README.md:140: 'that the stock is not coupled in is the hypothesis behind the body's words'). The interpretive 'a reading' is the house term for how far a claim has been seen and is fine.

Extent ('its own continuation', 'self-concerned'): the class under which a line counts as continuing the same, and the relation along which its closure is taken. The theory says continuation is relative to a class (ONE-PAGE.md:17) and that which class is a center's is not derived.

A SLOT: ONE-PAGE.md:54 states the hole itself, so a new name would hide it. Fine where the basis is given in the sentence (ONE-PAGE.md:11: 'read as all that can affect it at some remove'). README.md:64 denies the closed self by theorem ('An absolute self … is not unwise but impossible') and README.md:118 names exactly what is denied ('a self in another sense, one with a nature no relation carries'): keep both.

findings.term: the rule (that selects) set against what it selects and against "its states"

examples.quote: how winning comes to buy power over the rule that selects
a turn has to change the rule, not only its states
A rule read from the share it raises can lock and outlive a growing loss it does not read

findings.states: The criterion (the respect in which courses are alike or differ for which goes on) is itself formed, step by step, from the share that went on. Criterion and share are two relata in one loop, differing in pace or grain, not a ruler and the ruled. 'Change the rule, not only its states' states: a change that the next forming of the criterion from the share undoes does not last; one that alters what the criterion is formed from does.

examples.quote: It forbids explanations, not observations

findings.states: A theorem holds of every case that meets its premises; where a premise fails, the conclusion no longer follows. A thesis 'forbids' a case where the case would contradict it (ONE-PAGE.md:22: 'a case T7 forbids … occurred'). Nothing stands over the cases.

findings.term: a selection as a doer with a reach: "A selection reaches what couples in", "kept or dropped together, however hard the selection presses"

examples.quote: ## 1. A selection reaches what couples in

findings.term: read / reads / reading / readings: one knower's verb for at least eight relations

examples.quote: Take four parts of one law, told apart only by which part's next state reads which
A reading is refutable where every run outside it has a horizon within which every agreeing run is outside
Where a supplied reading of the world by the state is kept by the update under every act

findings.states: Each sense is a stated relation: (a) a part or law 'reads' conditions: its next value depends only on them, going alike wherever they are alike (51, 158); (b) 'read off' / 'through a map': is a function of the map's value (42); (c) a 'reading' in §5: a class of histories (199); (d) a 'reading of the world by the state': a relation between states and the worlds each admits (530); (e) 'being read' in §11: the act at that occasion couples into a selection of the law (507); (f) a reader 'reading one condition a step': a schedule of couplings (88); (g) 'read as': interpreted as; (h) '**Reading** [AI reading, …]': the page's own label for how far a statement has been seen.
findings.note: Count: read 132 + reads 39 + reading 276 + readings 46 (62 of 'reading' are the status label). The verb is defined relationally wherever a theorem uses it, so the split is not in the mathematics; it comes from the word: an eye-and-page figure is the chapter's main verb, and the same word names the account's dependence relation, a set of histories, an evaluator's coupling and the epistemic status of the paragraph. Sense (a) can be said one for one as 'depends only on'; (c) as 'class of histories'; (h) needs its own label. Kind is NAME for the verb; the noun 'reader' is the next finding.

findings.term: a formation with its own model facing a world: model / world, right / wrong, "the world answers"

findings.states: One joint law with parts. The 'model' is the list of candidate laws still agreeing with the answers so far, i.e. a lumping of what could answer; the 'world' is the part of the joint law whose next value depends on the act. 'Right along the course and wrong off it': the candidate and the answering part agree at the steps the course passes through and differ at steps it does not pass through. Line 537 says it as one relation: "the lumping the model keeps is the lumping its own choices make."

'World' (capital, 28) is the name of a model type and is not the finding; 'worlds' as candidate answerings (two worlds alike on a known act) is a third sense. Line 527 denies the subject facing a world and §12 then writes every theorem as formation and world, each with possessions ('its model', 14; 'on its own model'; 'the agent's model', 4). The pair is two parts of one law compared along one course; line 555's "two roles told apart by the paths of sensing and control" shows how to state the basis.

Which relation and which class draw the line is not derived.
findings.note: own 128, self 102, one's/oneself 119, de se 45, de dicto 5, boundary 13. Mostly the basis is stated and the word is then fine (line 16: 'A *center* is a formation; its own region is its closure under some relation of the unfolding'; line 355 P2: 'What is "one's own" is a region drawn along a relation of the unfolding'; line 463: 'The root reads every subject as continuation relative to a class'). The split is presumed where 'self' comes before any relation: 'the self's presupposition' (line 325), 'wanting one's own continuation' (line 204), 'self-significance'. 'De se / de dicto' is a POINTER to the philosophy of language used 50 times with a gloss (line 348) and no attribution; its gloss 'ascribes the property to its own center' is itself subject and predicate.

findings.term: normative premises against hypotheses about the unfolding; 'evaluative parameter'; 'reads only the dynamics'

no statement reading only the dynamics and holding of some dynamics entails the condition, by construction of the representation

findings.states: In the World model sig (and an order) is an argument that no statement about webs and flows varies with, so nothing about the flows implies anything about it. findings.term: admits / admitted / admission (levels as a gate); requires / requirement

findings.note: admit*/admission 180, require*/requirement 42. Defined as a relation at first use, so it misleads little by itself; it is listed for its frequency and because the gate picture leaks once into an argument (lines 437-448: 'imposed admission', 'left by a chooser or imposed'). Least urgent of the weight-2 findings.

findings.term: the condition asks / C asks / forces / permits / forbidden / verdict (a statement as ruler)

findings.states: 'The condition asks X' states that the condition holds only where X. 'Forces every center to coincide' states that where it holds on a net with no cycle, there is one center. 'Permits ending' states that under that significance the course that ends it loses nothing with significance. 'Verdict' states which of the four cases holds of a pair, or whether a pair is in an order.
findings.note: ask* 45 (21 with the condition, C, a theorem, P2 or the reach as subject); verdict 20; must 13; force 5; permits/forbidden/allows/ban 6; privileg* 6 (section 4.2's argument, Parfit's and Gewirth's setting). One-for-one replaceable; light but everywhere in sections 3 and 4.

findings.term: the rule (control of the rule, the rule still reading, the rule's; a tower of rules, each changing as the one above allows)

every rule changing only as the one above it allows and none the last, the scheme fixed

findings.note: rule(s) 49: about 14 are 'the rule' of alignment (lines 7, 216-243), 34 are the process sense in lines 116-118 (RuleTower and its moves), where the word is technical and the kind is NAME with lens 7 (tower, top, height, above). findings.term: rival (of the condition); 'the hard rival'

informed harm (a harmful arrangement kept knowingly, no loss returning), the hard rival

findings.term: law (stragglers after the 13 November change, and model premises named laws)

examples.quote: That every World law reads only the dynamics is a fact about the representation
Let the rest follow a law of what has stood reading through coupling, and both courses be feasible, so that each course and its balanced levels come from the laws.
The carrier flows give from nothing, so they do not meet the first law.

findings.states: Four uses still call a proved statement a law (lines 27, 96 'Its order laws are widening's', 106 'law 1's one-pair form', 444 'In [the law above]'): these state theorems. 'The first law' (4) and 'the law of exchange' (1) state premises of the model: nothing is given from nothing, every change of a level is what is taken and given. 'A law of what has stood' (4, with line 88) states how what a formation takes and gives at a step depends on the levels so far, with 'follow' adding the ruled.
findings.note: Fine uses: 'as a way of seeing and not as a law' (line 5, a denial); 'Kauffman's tentative law' (line 133, a pointer); 'a system's law' (line 5, section 7's term). 'no law of the dynamics fixes which' (line 355) denies a law while presuming the dynamics have them.

findings.term: represented boundary matches / recognizes its target / holding or recognizing it

examples.quote: Where its represented boundary matches what it depends on, a loss returns to it through its feeders

'Holding it does not guarantee acting on it' states that the response does not follow from the reading alone (the test: 'told of the bed, one model of two kept it').
findings.note: represent* 12, recogni* 3. Most 'represented dynamics / the representation' uses are the account speaking of its own model and are fine. The finding is section 3.3's opening, which frames route (b) with an inner picture set against what is there. 'Real in what it conditions' in the same sentence is the relational phrase to keep.

findings.term: second-order / one level up / meta-attractor / mechanism

examples.quote: it does not give the second-order direction of widening: a range whose widening keeps widening, compared with one merely wider now, stays open

'One level up' states that a sorting is itself among what a sorting sorts: the shapers' selection of the rule. 'Meta-attractor' states what line 5 says in plain words: control over a selection comes to be selected, and locks.

findings.term: holds / held (one word for five relations, one of them possession)

examples.quote: where it is a life in the joint selection, and not the rule, that holds a self-concerned order, what the closed relation buys is that life's reach, not the selection's
The class of one's line holds one's effects: everything one conditions is alike to oneself.
A living claim is *held* when it lies in some standpoint's own region.

findings.states: Five relations share the word: a statement is true somewhere ('the condition holds where'); a class or region contains ('holds one's effects' = everything one conditions is alike to oneself); something is kept fixed ('the held possible'); a significance is taken at a center ('held de se'); and a life or standpoint possesses an order or a valuation ('holds an order', 'holds significant'). Only the last brings in a holder and a thing held.
findings.note: 305 by grep; the possessive sense is about 15 (estimated; 5 matched a narrow pattern). Line 7 above also carries a market word ('buys'); cost/pay/buy 8 and gain 13 in these lines, most of them inside the chooser route, where they belong to the field pointed at.

findings.term: field terms used as pointers: chooser, menu, payoffs, Nash, Pareto; task, performer, substrate; born, birth; agents, principal, optimizers

examples.quote: A chooser here is a pair of values, and none is asserted to exist
Constructor theory's task, what performs it and the possible are read on any process divided by two readings, the performing part and the substrate
A stone goes on and ranks nothing, a system kept by its environment ranks nothing, and an agent may be indifferent between two courses

findings.states: The first two point at decision theory and constructor theory, name them (line 455: Foster, Nehring and Puppe, Strotz, the prisoner's dilemma; line 126), and say the doer as a reading of one process. Line 287 is not a pointer: it sorts stone, system-with-environment and agent as three kinds with no relation named; it states that going on, being sustained and taking one of two courses do not yet give a relation on courses.
findings.note: chooser 25, agent 4, principal 1, optimiz* 3, environment 1; the constructor-theory and causal-set terms are confined to lines 126-133 and attributed. All fine as attributed except line 287 (local, weight 1) and 'principal' in line 5, which is tagged [AI reading, D68] but not attributed to its field.

kept: Much of this half already says relations in the root's words, and these should be kept as the pattern for re-saying the rest. (1) The opening of section 4 and the thesis: "A life goes on through what sustains it, and going on is not yet an order over courses" (lines 5, 287). (2) The definitions that name the relation first: "A *center* is a formation; its own region is its closure under some relation of the unfolding" (16); "The root reads every subject as continuation relative to a class: an occurrence continues another where it is conditioned by it and alike to it under a class" (463); P4, "everything one conditions is alike to oneself" (533); "Whatever no chain joins" (548). (3) Pairs said as one relation with its cases: widening, keeping the same and mixed (57), with "Widening and narrowing are more and less future ... patterns within becoming, not good and evil" (90), and route (b) and the condition as "one presupposition ... at narrow and at wide scope" (333). (4) Selection said without a doer: "histories alike through every member's couplings at every step are selected alike" (233), "A selection is said to select for what it holds at; nothing here fixes which way a selection goes" (230), "Coupling a loss in is not depending on it" (7), and the first step apart and point of no return of section 3.6. (5) Comparisons that say by which comparison and from where: "a further judgment names its criterion and who holds it" (57), "The theorems show a mixed part mixed and weigh it for no one" (57), "\"better\" is free" (296), "Offered by us ... as a way of seeing and not as a law" (5). (6) The status marking, which is how the page keeps its slots visible: "is not shown" (17 times), "supplied" (24), the 40 "[AI reading ...]" tags, "The sorting is of the account's statements, not of what is in the unfolding" (37), "a fact about the representation" (27), and "Read so, the condition has no significance parameter: it is true or false once the net, the class and the centers are given" (466). The `living` reading is likewise marked as a choice (223). The word "read/reading" as the account's own marker of from where a thing is said is a strength; the trouble is only its second use for what a selection does. The root's own words are already frequent here (condition 400, class 196, reach 176, line 142, closure 113, alike 93, depend 65), mostly from section 4.5 on; the dualist shapes are concentrated in the Thesis, "Within the whole map", and the prose that opens or closes sections 3.3, 3.5 and 3.6.
top_three: The selection as doer with a beyond (lines 5, 7, 241, 243): 'what a selection reaches', 'the drain beyond what it reads', 'a selector reads what it drains', 'removes its own readers'. It frames the chapter's front paragraphs and is a construction; what it states is two relations on one net (drawing on, coupling into), one holding where the other does not, and sections 3.5-3.6 already say it that way.

The supplied slots said in possessive and attitude words: 'has significance from a standpoint', 'whose losses count', 'concern', 'a life forms or holds an order', 'one's own'. These mark what the account takes as given (the free sig, which relation and class is a center's own, whether any center carries an order); renaming would hide the holes. The tied, relational forms exist (own closure on the root, line 466; an order as a relation containing widening) and can lead, with the slot stated once.

Knower words for a dependence: 'reads', 'reader', 'sees', 'blind', 'tells apart' said of a selection, rule, group or gauge (about 34 uses plus 16 'reader'), sharing the word 'read' with the account's own interpretive marker (about 287 uses). What is stated is that a sorting comes out differently where something differs, and by which step.

findings.term: an optimum / optimization drains (lowers, breaks, takes, ends) what lies beyond its couplings

examples.quote: *Optimization drains what lies beyond its couplings, where that gives room.*
what a pool of selectors reaches, and, with room, what an optimum drains beyond what couples in
with room, every optimum lowers what lies beyond its couplings as far as any eligible outcome does
What every optimum does, exactly

findings.states: By the page's own definition (line 178) an optimum is an eligible outcome that no eligible outcome ranks above; it is a set of levels, and does nothing. The order depends only on the levels of one family of conditions (it rises with them) and goes alike whatever the other levels are. Where every eligible outcome standing higher at a condition not in the family is exceeded on the family by another eligible outcome (room, for instance where units are shared), the unbeaten outcomes are exactly those with that condition at the least level any eligible outcome has. So: a level that makes no difference to the order, and shares units with levels that do, stands at its least among the unbeaten outcomes.
findings.note: 31 = grep of optimum/optima followed by an action verb (19 lines); also 'every optimum' 26, drain* 49 on 22 lines. This is the 12 November shape (doer, done-to, beyond) and it is the chapter's thesis, its 'Where this chapter sits', the title of section 7's theorem, the table header and thesis T3. 'its couplings' gives couplings to an outcome, which has none; they are the order's family. Swapping 'drains' for another verb keeps the grammar; the sentence has to start from the order and the unbeaten outcomes, as line 181 already does ('Every order rising with a family has its optima at the least level beyond ... exactly where ...'). The anchor ids and Lean names (rise_paid_from_beyond, favours_reaching_beyond) are frozen and will keep the old shape.

findings.term: a selection / pool / proxy that reaches, tells apart, leaves unseen, is blind to

examples.quote: A selection through couplings, whether a reward, a training run, a market or natural selection, reaches only what couples into its selector
past the slack there, a dependence breaks unseen by every selection rewarding the rise
a pool tells apart what some member tells apart, and no more
This is the proxy problem as the account's theorem, in its blindness to what a proxy does not register

findings.states: A selection is a statement about histories (or flows) that holds alike on any two histories the couplings leave alike. For a pool: two histories are alike through the pool where every member couples them alike, and some selection holds at one and fails at the other exactly where some member does not couple them alike (lines 263, 266). 'Unseen': the breaking of that dependence makes no difference to any selection that holds only where the family rises. Nothing faces anything; there is a class of histories that go alike.
findings.note: 36 = tells apart 13 + unseen/blind/sees/observed/register 11 + selection as subject of an action verb 7 + selector 5 (each grep-counted). The page has the relational wording next to it ('couples them alike / apart', 9 times; 'selected alike', 'separates'), so 'tells apart' could go one for one to 'couples apart'; but 'reaches only what couples into its selector' and 'unseen by every selection' need re-saying. 'Selector' names a thing with an inside that couplings go 'into'.

findings.term: read / reads / reading / reader (three senses in one word)

examples.quote: every score that reads the condition only from the rest's end on scores them alike, however the member's act differs
Suppose nothing a learner reads tells two values of a choice apart: not its reward, not the dynamics, not its inputs.
*Readers reading readers.* Members act in turn, each by its law on what couples into it and on the acts before it
minimizing free energy cannot break a symmetry its law keeps, cannot read a drain it does not couple to

findings.states: In the formation sense: a formation's exchange (or a score, a rule, a learner's update) depends on a level, and goes alike on histories its coupling leaves alike. Line 276 states exactly this: 'Reading through a coupling is an inclusion of its class in exchanging alike on level histories.' In the interpretive sense: the text takes a statement of another field as a case of a theorem here, and says whose the correspondence is.
findings.note: 222 = reads 44 + read 61 + reading 104 (108 less 4 inside 'Spreading') + reader(s) 13, grep-counted. Estimated split: about 80 are the text's own interpreting ('[AI reading' 23 labels, '**Reading**' 19 headers, 'Read on/in/as' 11, 'read as' 12, 'a supplied reading') and about 140 say a formation, rule, score, law, learner or descent 'reads' a level. A third sense is a quantity taken as a function ('offspring a supplied reading'). The interpretive sense is fine and worth keeping: it marks a reading as a reading and attributes it (line 91). The formation sense is the finding: it puts a knower in front of a known where the theorem has a dependence, and because the same word also names the author's act, a reader cannot tell a level's making a difference from someone interpreting. In the formation sense it is replaceable by 'depends on' / 'goes alike on', with line 276 as the definition.

findings.term: optimizer, chooser, drawer's best response, ranks, rewarded, prefers: the order as a given

examples.quote: An optimizer ranks outcomes by what couples into it: a fisher rewarded by its catch ranks every uncaught unit higher caught
What protects what lies beyond at the set point is the choice among equal optima, which no theorem here models.
Such a chooser escapes the optimizer's drive at its set point, not the drain below it, nor joint excess.

findings.states: The theorems take an order on a set of eligible outcomes and speak of the outcomes no eligible outcome ranks above. How a formation's course comes to go by an order, and which unbeaten outcome a course goes to, is supplied and not derived: 'orders, capacities, horizons, pools and waiting are supplied' (430); 'how formations come to hold such scopes and orders is the open target' (13); 'It does not show which optimum is taken' (192).
findings.note: 115 = optimizer 16 + optimization/optimizing/optimized 12 + ranks/ranking/ranked 22 + best response 13 + preference words 19 + choice/choose words 37 minus overlaps not removed; reward words are a further 43. The agent words (an optimizer that ranks, a chooser that picks, a drawer whose rule responds) stand where the account has a hole it states openly. A new name would hide the hole; what is there to say is 'given an order' each time, with the open item pointed to. 'Rule' in 'a drawer's rule is a best response' is game theory's strategy and fine as that.

findings.term: beyond / the beyond / outside (a class said as a place)

examples.quote: A rise of what a group couples into, where a containing family gains nothing, is paid from beyond
the beyond falls by at least the rise

A family and its beyond are *set apart* where the formations taking part, and the family with the beyond, are listed without repetition, the beyond lies apart from the family and the family holds a condition.
replenishment from outside the whole

findings.states: Relative to a named group, the conditions of a containing family fall into two classes under one relation: those some member couples into, and those no member couples into. Under balance, where nothing comes into the containing family, the first class's stock after a step is at most its stock before plus what is taken from the second. The two classes are two ends of 'couples into', drawn for that group; line 166 shows this by re-drawing it inside a pair ('Read with the receiver as the family and the giver as the beyond').
findings.note: 149 = beyond 124 (46 lines) + outside 25 (17 lines). Of 'beyond': 23 are 'condition(s)/dependence(s) beyond' inside theorem statements whose hypotheses state the basis ('a condition no member of the group couples into', line 155) and are fine; 13 are the noun 'the beyond'; 8 'lies beyond'; 8 'from beyond'; 8 'reach(es) beyond'. The finding is the noun and the lead sentences, where a place stands in for the class. 'Outside' has the same grammar (the 1 November swap): 'renewed from outside', 'taught from outside', 'outside the whole' mark the edge of a model, each relative to a list, but 'outside the whole' gives the whole an outside. The page's own phrase 'conditions no member couples into' says the class by its relation; line 358 does the same for 'external'.

findings.term: formation takes from / gives to a condition; role nouns in -er (taker, drawer, giver, keeper, renewer, dweller, holder)

examples.quote: In a minimal witness two takers end themselves and their renewer, one taker does not.
A collective can keep itself by consuming others, whose renewal is asked at a named class and grain
In Diversion the store's rise ends the dweller, unseen by the selection through the taker

findings.states: The World model has two sorts: formations (active or not, they end) and conditions (they have levels). Balance is the one relation between them: 'every change of a condition's level is what those taking part take and give' (13). A role noun names one end of that exchange at a step, and the same formation stands at several ends: 'a taker among them where it so depends' (27), 'Both draw alike, so a keeper draws on what it keeps' (412). Line 29 states: with two formations each taking within what a step gives, the level stays below the need and every formation depending on it at that need is inactive, those two and the one giving to it among them.
findings.note: 205 = grep of 26 role stems + er(s) on 74 lines; formation(s) 133, condition(s) 122, take* 120, give* 167, draw* 185. The two sorts are the model's, and the page says most theorems here are on the World and not on the root's grammar (13, 434), so this is a stated given, not a slip; renaming would hide that the taker / taken-from split is not derived from the one relation here. The local findings are the sentences where a role noun becomes a kind of thing that acts on another or on itself ('end themselves', 'keep itself by consuming others', 'the rise ends the dweller'). The verbs take/give themselves are fine: two signs of one exchange.

findings.term: paid from, pays, price, costs, free to, worth, forgoes (market words for balance)

that more waiting gives no more is the structural price of complexity
Renewal from outside can make a gift free to the giver's level; what it costs the giver's line is a further part, `γ`, which can be nothing.

findings.states: 'Paid from': under balance a rise at one family is at most what is taken from the other conditions (the clause after the colon at 155 already says it). 'Price': under added waits, whatever gives gives without them, at every step. 'Costs': the difference in a line's level between keeping an amount and giving it.

'Gains nothing' (12) and 'what the whole loses' are arithmetic of levels and fine. The finding is the section-6 headline and the readings, where a transaction (payer, price) is laid over a balance.

it comes to couple into a loss only as its course without the loss would
A real loss need not form a [meta-attractor](02-MAP.md#r-closed-capture)

findings.term: law (what a formation follows, holds, is under); one leftover 'the law' for a theorem

examples.quote: where the rest follows one law of exchange reading through coupling
the kind does not rise, whatever laws it holds and whatever the errors
a pair of such laws withholds at every step from the first of them on
([the law](#r-what-an-optimum-does-beyond-what-couples-in))

findings.states: How a formation's giving (or exchange) at the next step depends on what gave at this one: a constancy, alike starts going alike. Line 116 says it without the word: 'Let each formation give at a step according to whether what it waits on gave.' Nothing is followed or held; the dependence is the formation's going.
findings.note: 102 occurrences on 56 lines (grep, word-bounded). Four senses: (a) a step map, the bulk ('law of giving', 'law of exchange', 'a law keeping the exchange'), a usual mathematical word, but here with 'follows', 'under', 'holds' and once as an actor ('laws withholds'); (b) a probability distribution, 10 times in lines 332 and 334 ('an exchangeable law'), probability's own term and fine; (c) the account's proved statement, left from before 13 November: line 238 '[the law]', 415 'The law of a revision is the region', 423 'laws for states with gaps', 434 'shared-law lines', and the anchor ids ending in -laws; (d) 'a law of logic' (111), 'not a universal law' (394). kept: Chapter 01 is where the account's relational saying is strongest, and most of it should stand as it is. (1) Every sameness is said with its class and every position relative to one: 'beginning, abiding, altering and ending are positions relative to a class, none standing alone' (5), 'Renewal is said with its class or not at all' (145), 'Continuation is a relation, not an identity' (65). (2) Pairs said as one relation with two ends: 'formations and conditions are two roles of one relatum' (191); 'what the part does is what the rest undergoes, by definition' (486), with the theorem that one course does not fix whose move it is; 'Law and history are one unfolding read two ways, the law read off the unfolding rather than set over it' (477); 'structure and change are one lumping' (171); 'influence and reach point opposite ways' (597); renewal without end and ceasing as greatest family and inductive dual (149); a law with noise 'is a relation of exchange' (225), which dissolves signal against noise. (3) Separateness shown, not presumed: 'no frame or kind of thing is chosen before the relations' (20); the carrier 'not a claim that its elements exist apart from their relations' (33); 'a feedback loop is a line returning to a class, not an occurrence reaching itself' (39); 'Separation loses exactly the relation' (467); 'Labels carry nothing' and identity as 'one reading of continuation, not a fact beneath it' (579, 582); the step index 'a reading of the relations, not their ground' (553). (4) Inside and outside given their basis: the Boundaries reading (611 to 617), 'It is no further thing or relation beside what it delimits', 'Which boundaries a formation has depends on the relation followed', 'A boundary short of the whole is real … and relative to that relation', and the rest of the whole 'counted as one more relatum' (265). (5) Comparison with its basis: a result that ranks courses 'states what its theorem takes as hypotheses' (11, 434). (6) The honest marks of what is given and not derived (equality on the carrier, amounts, which class, requirement beyond the course, 'supplied' 13 times, the 'not shown' lists) are part of the map and should not be renamed away. Lenses 3, 6 and 8 are nearly empty here: no govern, obey, enforce, constraint, proxy, principal, aligned, goal or purpose in the account's own voice.
top_three: 'reads' with a law, relation, level or part as the knower (16 sentences, and the verb read 229 times in all): each sentence states a dependence ('depends only on', 'is the same for', 'makes no difference to') and can be said so one for one; this is the root page's most frequent fallback and it feeds 'reader' and 'the loss it does not read' in the later chapters.

The class as asked, chosen or named ('the sameness asked', 'the grammar names the class and does not choose it', 'observer-dependence is the choice of class'): a SLOT at the centre of 'continuation relative to a class'. The relation does not fix the class, and the wording puts an unnamed asker there; a new word would hide the hole, so the gap (what a class depends on, how a sameness forms) should be stated as open.

'Law' standing before its course: 'the course a law generates', 'a law giving back what it takes', 'a law must break the symmetry', 'the law of change stays fixed', against the page's own 'the law read off the unfolding rather than set over it'. The acting verbs can be re-said ('a run of', 'along'); what remains is a real given (the moves not taken, requirement, the fixed scheme), and the same word still names proved statements about 32 times after the 13 November change.

findings.term: a selection that reaches, drains, reads, locks on what it already chose (the centre sentence and the four questions)

examples.quote: what a selection (a reward, a judge, a market, a vote, a training run) reaches, what it drains beyond what it reads, how it comes to lock on what it already chose
what it reads or needs, what lies beyond that, whether it can do better on what it reads by lowering what lies beyond, and whether its rule can lock on what it already selected
a selection can meet its own criterion while what it cannot read is lost

findings.states: Outcomes that are alike in everything that couples into a selecting go alike under it (同行). So a condition that does not couple in makes no difference to what is selected, while what is selected still makes a difference to that condition. With room, the outcomes an order ranks highest are ones where dependences on such conditions break. Where the rule is formed from the share already selected, share and rule condition each other and the course keeps coming back to the same favouring.
findings.note: Count is 'a selection / any selection / joint selection' (grep); the same shape also runs through 'drain' (16), 'reach' in the selection sense (6 of 27) and 'chose/selected' at USES:9 and :15. The noun 'selection' is made the doer, with a thing done to and a place it does not get to. The pages already hold the relational statement and can be said from it: USES-EXAMPLES.md:35 ('Two histories are selected alike by every selection through a formation's couplings exactly when they are alike through them') and USES.md:28 ('every optimum of an order rising with what couples in breaks exactly the dependences beyond that some eligible outcome breaks'). Swapping 'drains' or 'reaches' for another verb keeps the doer; the sentence has to be said again from those two.

where nothing in the loop reads what lies beyond the share, the lock outlives any loss it does not read

findings.states: A one-way conditioning: these are conditions the selecting makes a difference to and that make no difference to it. There is no place 'beyond'; the line is drawn along coupling. 'Beyond the share' states that the rule depends on nothing but the share it favours, so what happens to those it does not favour does not come back into it.

findings.states: Four different relations: (a) 'X reads Y': what is selected differs when Y differs, Y couples in; (b) 'the rule is read from the share': the rule depends on the share, is formed from it; (c) 'a Reading / AI reading / read on the map': this placing of a case under a theorem's class is an interpretation, not proved; (d) 'readers drawn from the selected': the members whose kind's return forms the rule.
findings.note: 379 word-forms by grep (100 / 203 / 76). By pattern: about 115 with a selection, judge, rule or loop as the one that reads; 25 'read from'; about 97 as the label or 'a reading'; 40 'reader(s)'. 'Reads' sets the selection up as a knower facing a text. The theory's own word is coupling, and USES.md:27 gives the gloss 'what a selector reads or needs': 'reads' alone drops 'needs', the dependence half, which is not knowing. In USES.md:29 senses (a) and (b) sit in one sentence. Sense (c) is fine as a label, and (d) is the model's term with its basis stated. For (a) and (b) the one-for-one words exist on the page: 'couples in', 'is formed from', 'depends on'.

At a step the rule favours the shapers (weakly) exactly where the cost `c` is at most what comes back to them alone

findings.term: rules out / forbids / prohibition / no guarantee; verdict

examples.quote: Together they rule out a guarantee from the theory, however much is observed
the account reaches farther in what it forbids than a few frameworks and the free-energy principle alone, each prohibition known in a neighbouring field
across a stretch the shared part can turn the verdict

findings.states: For a theorem: under these hypotheses no course of this kind occurs in the model. For a thesis: it says no case of this class occurs, and one occurring counts against it. For the guarantee: no statement from these theorems entails that every collective's course widens.
findings.note: 44 = rule(s) out / forbid / guarantee 17 plus 'verdict' 27 (grep). After 'law' became 'theorem', the theorems still act as rulers: §3 of COLLECTIVE-DIRECTION is headed 'What the theory's own theorems rule out' with a column 'What it rules out'. 'Forbids' for a thesis is the idiom of falsification, used without attribution. One for one: 'excludes', 'has no such case', 'says does not occur'. 'Verdict' is fine for a frozen test's outcome (criterion fixed before the run, and said) and in 'a way of seeing, not a verdict', which denies the ruler; EXAMPLES:109 uses it for which kind the rule favours, a slip, and COLLECTIVE-DIRECTION:26 heads its table of the three senses with it.

(1) Alike goes alike, with no doer: USES-EXAMPLES.md:35 'Two histories are selected alike by every selection through a formation's couplings exactly when they are alike through them', and USES.md:28 on the optimum breaking dependences. (2) The ethics paragraph (USES.md:15, COLLECTIVE-DIRECTION.md:32): 'A life goes on through what sustains it', 'where relations of being affected close', costs that 'come back to it' or 'never come back', 'where they run one way'; EXAMPLES:24 'The bed gives the fishers nothing, so here relations run one way'. This is the root's grammar and is the model for re-saying the centre and the aim. (3) COLLECTIVE-DIRECTION.md:9 'A collective is part of the world it would move, so the question asks of the collective's course'. (4) Pairs said as one relation: 'widening is a relation between two courses on which every such weighting agrees, not a quantity to maximize' (CD:37); 'control and lock are one loop on either side of a critical mass' (CD:44); 'a rule rebuilt from the members it limits' (CD:91); 'Starting from relations removes the frame of a fixed sum divided among independent owners. It does not remove rivalry' (CD:119). (5) Knowing as relation: 'reading a loss, counting it and ranking courses are separate relations'; 'knowing another's law is no coupling'; observation as only the first of six conditions, each a relation (coupling, response, time, resolution, pace, structure). (6) Test 4 is met almost everywhere: 'a result that ranks names the order its theorem takes', 'the theorems weigh them for no one', 'none says restraint is better or cooperation good', T8 as 'a way of seeing, not a verdict' with 'who bears it'. 'Must' occurs nowhere. (7) Words that look suspect and are fine here: 'couples in' and 'closure' (the line's relation is stated), 'the rest' (the other drawers on the same condition), 'within becoming' and 'no should beyond becoming' (denials of an outside), 'level' (an amount), 'independent causes' and 'conditional independence' (technical), 'correspondence' and 'bridge' (whether a case meets a theorem's hypotheses, said so at CD:92), the count model's 'shapers' and 'others' (two kinds whose basis is a stated premise), and the standing labels Proved, Tested, Reading, Argued, Open.
top_three: A selection made the doer: 'what a selection reaches, what it drains beyond what it reads, how it comes to lock on what it already chose' (USES.md:9, the four questions at :15, and the aim sentence 'design an alignment that keeps humans and AI ... out of'). The grammar carries the split; the relation is already on the page at USES-EXAMPLES.md:35 and USES.md:28.

'beyond', 'what lies beyond', 'the beyond', 'beyond its own share': 45 uses in the selection sense. It states a one-way conditioning (the selecting makes a difference there, and nothing there makes a difference to it) as a territory; fine only where the relation is named ('beyond what couples in').

The rule as a ruler and the loop as a contest: 'winning comes to buy power over the rule that selects', 'the rule favours', 'capture', 'control of the rule'. The theorems state a return (share conditions rule, rule conditions share) with nothing standing over it, and the pages themselves say the models do not tell capture from accountable revision.

findings.term: "every optimum drains what its order does not read" (an outcome made a doer, an order made a reader)

examples.quote: with room every optimum drains what its order does not read
So with room, if the boats can take the stock below the seabirds' need, every optimum does.
T3 says which way an optimizer goes, which is no verdict.

findings.states: Among the eligible outcomes, one that no eligible outcome is ranked above stands at the least eligible level at every listed condition the ranking does not depend on, given room (any outcome standing higher there is exceeded, on what the ranking depends on, by another eligible outcome). An outcome does nothing and an order perceives nothing: the relation is between a ranking, the conditions it depends on, and levels at the conditions it does not depend on.
findings.note: Count is 'optimum/optima' as the subject of a doing verb in ONE-ARGUMENT (grep); drain/empty forms occur 20 times there, optim* 46. This is the page's one sentence: its italic summary, its step table and the theorem's name all carry doer + knower + beyond together. The page already has the relational form at :39 ('every optimum of every rising order stands, at each condition beyond, at the least level among the eligible outcomes') and in the Lean (`Least rest eligible o`); the summary sentence has to be said again from that, not re-worded. 'Drain' is fine where boats take fish (a flow from a stock); it is the split when an optimum or an order is its subject.

findings.term: "the beyond", "beyond its couplings", "draws from beyond" (a place past a selection)

examples.quote: **The family and the beyond.** The *family* is what couples into the selection (the catch); the *beyond* is listed conditions that do not (the stock). Beyond is no place: the selection fixes it.
what optimizing drawers do beyond their couplings
the drain lying where what lies beyond shares units with what is rewarded.

findings.states: One relation, coupling into the order: a listed condition either is one the ranking (or the offspring count) depends on, or is one the outcomes depend on and the ranking does not. Room says the second kind exchanges units with the first, so what is called beyond is joined to the family by exchange; it is 'the conditions the order does not depend on', not somewhere outside.
findings.note: 55 occurrences of 'beyond' in the three pages; 27 in this sense (ONE 15, 04 10, FEP 2), 10 inside link paths and anchors, the rest plain 'further than' ('beyond the linear case', 'beyond one lemma'), which is fine. findings.states: The ratio in force is the count-weighted mean of fixed ratios (u, v; hi, lo, lo'), weighted by how many members of each kind there are; a 'reader of the loss' is a term of that mean that depends on the second coordinate from N on; 'removed' = the term is absent once the coordinate passes K. How a member comes to carry a ratio, and that it carries one favouring its own kind, is given, not derived.
findings.note: The word brings a subject (a mind that perceives) into a model whose 'readers' are weights in a mean. The chapter marks the hole honestly ('who such readers are, is not established', line 459; LA2 found a trained judge is not such a pool, line 446). A new name would hide it; what needs saying each time is that the slot is given. §10 already turns the knower-known shape round and should be kept: the readers' 'standing hanging on what the loss takes' (476), 'readers of what lies beyond a share are removed by what they read' (476): the one that reads depends on what is read.

findings.term: what lies beyond the share / the beyond

examples.quote: With the fast configuration the share and what lies beyond it, where neither the next share nor the rule read reads the beyond (`Unread`), courses alike in share and rule stay alike
where none is present the rule read is theirs, so a reader of the beyond present and reading otherwise
the shapers' share draws on what lies beyond it; what it draws removes those whose standing hangs on it, and they are the rule's readers of that loss

findings.states: A second coordinate of the same configuration that the share's step and the ratio do not depend on. In §10 the share's course raises it ('draws on' it) and in §11 it is a level the going on needs: the share depends on it while its ratio does not. Nothing is outside anything; a dependence runs one way and not the other.
findings.note: 'beyond' occurs 81 times (grep); about 35 are this sense (estimated from a context listing; 'lies beyond' 21, 'the beyond' 7, 'beyond the share' 10). It is the word the 12 November finding named, and here it has become a noun. The separateness is presumed in §9 (the coordinate is simply the other half of a pair) and denied in §10-§11. Other uses are fine and should be told apart: a comparison along an amount ('drawing beyond renewal', 'beyond every bound', 'a net draw beyond this margin', 'beyond chance'), about 25; and membership of a finite family, where the basis is stated ('A family is *fed from beyond* across a step where a formation takes from outside it and gives to a member', line 163), about 15; scope ('beyond the models'), about 5. 'outside' (16) is mostly scope or family membership; 'a reader outside the share' (444) is this finding again.

findings.term: the capacity to shape the rule / shapers / control over the selection

examples.quote: On `RuleCapture`'s counts let the carriers be shapers: shaping gives `s` to the shapers alone and `p` to every member alike and costs each shaper `c`
`s` and `p` are constants of the rule, and the courses are without noise
the lock of the corpus's meta-attractor and its second order, the selection of control over the selection, are one loop where the rule's readers are drawn from those it selects

findings.states: Two kinds, one leaving a + s + p offspring a member and the other a + c + p; the first kind's share does not fall exactly where c ≤ s; with the ratio a count-weighted mean (hi where the first kind weighs, lo where the other does), the share rises above a critical ratio of counts and falls below it. That s comes from anything the first kind does to the ratio is not in the model: s, p, c are constants.
findings.note: 153 forms of shape/shaping/shaper(s) (shapers 97); 'capacity' 21; 'control' about 10 in this sense. The words name an agent with a power over a rule (and Reading 452 says 'a rule the shapers change'), while the theorem has a kind whose offspring count carries an extra constant. This is the phrase the project's aim leans on ('does not come to select for control over its own selection'), so what is proved and what is named differ most where it matters most. The honest sentences are there ('That offspring carry their parent's capacity, and that what comes back is read from the share, are premises'; 'The join of the two models takes the readers' premise as lo ≤ hi and does not select it'). What is missing is a derivation that what comes back depends on a change the kind makes to the ratio; renaming would hide that. 'What comes back to the shapers alone' already says the relation in the root's words and is kept.

findings.term: loss, as the name of the coordinate the loop does not depend on (§9-§10)

examples.quote: Evidence, refutation and institutions are unformalized, and the unread coordinate is a loss by reading.
from a locked configuration the loss passes every bound while the course stays locked and neither share nor rule falls below the start
The first is §9's and §10's lock outliving its loss, once what is lost is a level the going on needs

findings.states: In §9: a counter that rises by at least one a step. Whose it is and by which comparison it is a loss is not said there (test 4). §10 says on whom it falls (added to the other kind's count); §11 says what it is a loss of: the fall of a level that the going on needs.
findings.note: 'loss(es)' 157 on the page; 63 in §9 and 47 in §10 (awk by line range). Three senses, two of them fine: a possibility that can no longer be had (§2, defined: 's cannot be had again'), a fall of an amount (§4, 'least loss', defined), and this one, a value word laid on a bare coordinate. The page says so once (line 444) and then uses the word 110 times without the qualifier. The relation is available since 13 November (§11's level that the going on needs); until §9 is said on it, 'loss' there marks something given.

findings.term: selection / selects / selected as an actor

examples.quote: A selection rewarding a target raises its carriers' share
so the whole selects for shaping exactly where `c` times the spread of shaping falls short of `s` times it with `m q` times the spread among groups
a metric whose rule and reading are formed from the share it selects is kept by its selectors however large a loss it does not read grows

The chapter's own best sentence against it is line 489: 'No step of it needs a selection that prefers the removal or an optimizer aiming at it; it needs only that what is drawn falls on those who would read it.'

findings.term: rule (the rule favours, the rule in force, the rule keeps a reader)

examples.quote: The lock belongs to how the rule reads, not the share it favours
from the bound on, the rule keeps a reader of the loss beyond the share
At a step the rule favours the shapers (weakly) exactly where `c ≤ s`, whatever `p` comes to every member alike

findings.note: 144 of 219 in §9; 'rule in force' 22. The word sets something over the course that the course then obeys, where the model has one step on a pair. The chapter says the pair plainly three times and these should lead: 'A two-level course, the rule changing only at reading steps, is a run of one law' (385); 'exactly where the rule makes no difference to the state ... the rule is read in the state's regularity' (439); 'the level in the place `adaptive` gives to what it calls the rule' (500); 'a tower of rules with no top is one process too' (441). findings.term: law (under a law, follows a law, a determined law) and four leftovers

examples.quote: Under a law some configurations come round again; what does not is drawn into a region it never leaves, the unfolding narrowing its own future.

Where the rest follows one law of exchange reading what has stood, two balanced flows with the same formations present, starting alike, in which the part acts alike, have the same levels and exchange at every step
No theorem states the law over real amounts

findings.states: Each configuration conditions exactly one next (§11's own words: 'A determined law's step has a fixed successor'); 'the rest follows a law of exchange' = what the rest exchanges at a step is a function of the levels so far.
findings.note: 110 by grep, about 30 inside Lean identifiers (`Law.…`), so about 80 in prose: mostly the step map (§2 16, §4 21, §7 29, §11 13). 'Under' and 'follows' give it the ruler's grammar, and it is the same word the 13 November pass took out of the proved statements, so a reader meets 'law' again two lines below 'theorem'. findings.term: favours / disfavours / cost / helps / hurts / in their favour

examples.quote: One more step before anything comes back never helps the shapers, and one more step with it never hurts them where it covers the cost
let selection not lower a target's share under a rule favouring it (`Raises`)
the course is locked in their favour for good from the next step

findings.states: A comparison of two counts at a step: this kind's members leave at least as many offspring as the other's. 'Cost' c and 'what comes back' s are constants added to the two counts; 'helps/hurts' = the share is not lower / not higher.
findings.note: favour* and disfavour* 103, cost 27, gain* 20. Each use is exactly defined (`favours_iff`), so nothing is wrong locally; the matter is that a count comparison is said 100 times as a benefit to someone, with no 'from where' (test 4), on the page that says 'The map orders nothing'. 'Cost' with Hamilton's rule is that field's term and attributed (424). 'What comes back' (32 times) is the root's own wording and is kept.

findings.term: capture; the lock as an actor (locks the course, outlives, draws its readers out)

examples.quote: *Readers the loss removes, and the lock drawing them out.*
That is no capture by the shapers but the same closed reading: every course read from the share alone is locked one way or the other
Selected control is not thereby capture, which the first condition, control of the rule not captured, excludes

findings.states: A region of configurations closed under the step, in which neither the share nor the ratio falls (510: 'the locked configurations form a region closed under the step'). It closes either way: below the critical ratio of counts the same closure holds for the other kind.
findings.note: capture* 38 (the title of §9 and seven record names), lock* 124, outliv* 7. 'Capture' needs a captor and a captive, and the text has to take it back twice (454, 459) because the theorem is symmetric: every course whose ratio depends on the share alone is closed one way or the other. 'Lock' as a noun for the closed region is defined and serviceable; as a subject of verbs ('locks the course', 'outlives its loss', 'drawing them out', 'noise leaves either lock') it is the doer again.

findings.term: drawn into / attraction (§2), and 'draw' in three senses

examples.quote: a configuration is drawn into some absorbing region exactly where it does not return (`Law.drawn_iff_not_returns`), and once drawn never comes back
so a law that merges draws something, up to double negation
So a share not lower draws no less on what lies beyond, its loss not lower at every step, and its readers of it are therefore gone no later

findings.states: §2: a configuration does not come back exactly where its line reaches a region closed under the step that does not hold it. §3-§5: a draw is the amount taken from a condition across a step. §9: readers 'drawn from the selected' = the weights are the population's counts; 'drawn one at a time' = one member replaced a step with those weights.
findings.note: 212 forms of draw (§5 87, §9 61, §2 17, §10 17). Three different relations share the verb, and in §10 two of them meet in one sentence ('the lock drawing them out', 'draws on what lies beyond'). In §2 the passive presumes a puller (attract* 16, absorb* 8); the theorem is about reaching and not returning, and the page says so ('near-definitional, not a classical attractor'). The §3-§5 sense is defined at 248 and careful: 'It does not say the drawing made the deficit' (113).

findings.term: meta-attractor / every level of the loop / two-level / second order

examples.quote: **Definition.** 元吸引子 (yuán xīyǐnzǐ, meta-attractor): a loop of selection whose rule and whose reading of the rule are both formed from the share it selects
where every level of the loop reads only the share, a loss it does not read leaves it locked however large
A second order, corruption taking over courts, press, statistics and audit, is a loop whose rule-reading reaches the routes of 明 themselves

findings.states: One step on a configuration with a faster and slower coordinates (share; ratio; the weights by which the ratio is formed), each slower one a function of the share. Nothing stands above: 'a tower of rules with no top is one process too' (441).
findings.note: meta-attractor/元吸引子 about 10 in prose, 'two-level' 5, 'level of the loop' 2, second/third order 3 (sum of greps). 'Meta' and 'level of the loop' say tiers where the theorems say coordinates of one course. 'Level' is also the page's word for the amount of a condition (192 times) and both senses stand in one sentence at line 9. Meta-attractor is the corpus's own name and works as a pointer to it (448, 463 attribute it); the definition at 412 is where it should be said as one loop. 'Order k' in §1 and §7 (generation at order k, order j of the carried amount) is a count of steps of a relation and fine.

findings.term: degeneration (退化) beside generation

examples.quote: *degeneration* (退化, tuìhuà) is 尽

Arising is activity starting, not §1's generation; the records `unceasing-generation-needs-renewal` and `whole-persists-through-generation` are theorems on arising that keep "generation" only in their ids.
one set of selection laws can admit a protected and a degenerate region at once

findings.states: Three regions of one relation read at a coarse and a fine class together: the coarse line goes on with fine lines beginning ahead of every member; it goes on with none from some point; everything continuing the point ends (尽).
findings.note: The pair is said well as a relation (proved exclusions, a mixed region 生守相杂, 'renewal does not decide the region') and the order is disclaimed ('That generation is better than keeping or degeneration: no theorem says so', 530; 'Degeneration and dissolution belong to the unfolding as fully as generation', 61). The finding is only the name: 'degeneration'/退化 says a falling away from something better, where the definition is 尽, ends on every branch, and the title carries it. The 文言 terms (延, 尽, 传, 守) already name the regions without it. 'Generation' needed its own disclaimer at 151 and 61 ('it is not 生生').

findings.term: a measure and its refutation; evidence set against what the loop reads (T7)

examples.quote: **Thesis T7.** *A measure read from what it selects outlives its refutation*
is dropped only through a change in what the loop reads (a reader outside the share, a loss entering it, a new reading), not on evidence alone
"the metric survives its own refutation" is read as `lock_outlives_loss`, the refutation as a loss the loop does not read

findings.states: One relation with two ends: a difference changes the ratio only where the ratio depends on it. 'Evidence' that the ratio does not depend on and 'a loss it does not read' are the same thing; 'refutation' is that difference growing.
findings.note: metric 8, evidence 7, refutation 5. The thesis is worded as measure against truth (the proxy and the true objective under other names), with selectors who keep or drop. The page says that 'Evidence, refutation and institutions are unformalized'. Said as a relation the thesis is: such a ratio changes only through what it depends on.

findings.term: forbids / verdict / decides / fate / certifies

examples.quote: 守 forbids renewal throughout its family where 全守 allows an earlier one
so across a stretch the shared part can turn the verdict
the point decides the fate where the recent giving lies on the level's side

findings.states: 'Forbids' = excludes (§1's own word: 'exclude each other'); 'the verdict' of a theorem = which way the share moves; 'X decides Y' = Y holds exactly where X; 'fate' = whether a run ends; 'Persistence certifies the joint draw' (288) = what persists has had the joint draw within the margin.
findings.note: forbid* 19, verdict 13, fate 20, 'decides the/whether/for' and 'counts/start/score decide' 12, certif* 1. Told apart: '*Forbids*' and '*Refuted by*' as the fixed headings of a thesis, and 'verdict' for a frozen test's outcome, are the method's terms (08) and work as pointers; 'decided' in the constructive sense (about 42 of 54, with LPO) is technical and fine. The findings are the courtroom words inside theorems: line 40, 'either verdict' for a direction (424), 'the point decides the fate', 'the counts when they read it decide for good' (450).

findings.term: target / rewarding / seeker

examples.quote: Where target carriers each leave at least `a` offspring and other parents at most `b < a`
the seeker ends where it does not resume, no need supplied
无明 is seeking locked onto a target that cannot be met at rest

findings.states: 'Target' = the kind whose members leave more offspring; 'seeker' = a formation whose take is more than its last at every step (line 310 defines it so: 'A take more than now at every step').
findings.note: target 9, seek* 7, reward* 5 (some in link text). Purpose words on a kind and on a rising take. The 03 chapter owns 'seeking'; here it is a pointer to it.

findings.term: act / counterfactual / chooser / choice / policy

examples.quote: the counterfactual of an act is the course the law generates
*A chooser reading what couples in, its rule read from the count of its choices.*
a choice matters only at a juncture

findings.states: 'Act' = the part's exchange; two courses alike except in it. 'Choice' at a juncture = which of two steps the course takes, one after which s can still be had and one after which it cannot. 'Chooser' = a formation whose step is a function of the history of what couples into it.

'Counterfactual', 'policy' and 'chooser' point at causal inference and active inference and are attributed (461). §7's Reading already says the relation and is kept: 'neither is a second world: each is the law's step beyond its history' (369); 'the course without the act compares, it is no standard' (321).

findings.term: its own / itself / self- (the loop holds itself; rules that change themselves)

examples.quote: where the rule of selection is read from the share it selects, the loop holds itself
*Rules that change themselves, read in the grammar.*
the unfolding narrowing its own future

findings.states: A dependence that comes back: the ratio is a function of the share and the next share a function of the ratio. No self does the holding.
findings.note: own 54, itself/themselves 23, self- 12. Most are fine: a difference between a part's exchange and the joint exchange, whose basis is stated ('its own with every other drawer's', 288; 'keeps its own support and can still undermine another', 142), or a coupling whose two ends coincide ('self-loop'). The finding is the handful where a reflexive verb stands for a loop (398, 439, 66, 'self-keeping rule' at 80). The page answers one of them itself: 'a rule changing its own rule adds nothing to its whole possible' (441).

findings.term: blindness / visible / gives no warning / unforeseen

examples.quote: In the constructed draw the blindness before the break and the loop's forming are one event seen from two sides.
under a draw exceeding everything drawn before what stands gives no warning
Which a run shows is visible neither in one configuration nor in the drawer's own course: it belongs to the whole run and all that draws on the condition.

findings.states: Above its threshold a stock couples with strength zero: its distance to the break makes no difference anywhere ('the distance to the break is carried nowhere', 350). Renewing or consuming is a class of the whole run with all that draws on the condition, not of one configuration.
findings.note: Local. The second half of each sentence already says the relation ('it belongs to the whole run', 'carried nowhere', 'does not couple in'); the sight words are the first half.

findings.term: noise / drift as an actor

examples.quote: Noise leaves either lock: from every mixed count the histories losing every shaper weigh at least `down ^ i` times every later history
a lock kept in counts that only grow can survive noise

findings.states: The same weights taken two ways: as the exact proportions of the next population, or as the weights with which one member at a time is replaced. Taken the second way, histories leaving the closed region have positive weight.
findings.note: noise 19, drift 18. Population genetics' terms, used with their sources (Fudenberg and Imhof; Nowak) and fine as pointers. 'Without noise' is a stated premise each time. Only 'noise leaves', 'survive noise' make it a doer.

findings.term: representation / actual / model (a model set against what is actual)

examples.quote: *Open*: whether every becoming has a faithful representation in the grammar.
How a center represents the region is unmodelled
That actual rules read the share is the premise.

findings.states: Whether a case meets a theorem's premises is not derived; it is asked each time ('is not established', 'is not shown').

'Representation' at line 7 and 'represents' at 142 do bring a picture-and-pictured split; 08's 'reading' with its defeater is the repository's own way of saying it. findings.term: the corpus's words in Readings: winners, scorecard, power, corruption, lever, care

examples.quote: winners writing the next scorecard is `ReadsShare`, winners forming the minds that read it is `ReadsShare` on the reading
Its lever is exact at a step
Patterns of capture pass as patterns of care do.
