top_three: The centre sentence shape of §9-§10, repeated in the Thesis (line 7), 'Within the whole map' (line 9), the §9 opener (398), the definition of the meta-attractor (412) and T7 (444): an actor (selection, rule, loop, lock) that reads a share, does not read what lies beyond, locks the course and outlives a loss. It is a CONSTRUCTION: four splits in one sentence, and the chapter's own §11 (lines 439, 510, 525) already states it as a class that goes alike in a region closed under the step while another level changes and makes no difference to it. The front of the page has not caught up with its last section.

'read' and 'readers': 534 forms of read plus 127 of reader(s) against 43 of depend* and 6 of 'makes a difference'. Where a step, law or rule 'reads' a quantity the statement is dependence (NAME, about 200 uses); where 'readers' read, the word marks a SLOT (weights in a mean whose origin is a premise: 'who reads is a premise', 'That readers are minds is a reading'). With it goes 'the beyond' (about 35), the same non-dependence said as an outside.

'The capacity to shape the rule' / 'shapers' / 'selection of control over the selection' (153 forms): an agent's power is named where the model has two kinds with constant offspring counts ('s and p are constants of the rule'). It is a SLOT, and the one the project's stated aim leans on; beside it 'loss' in §9-§10 (110 uses) names a bare coordinate by a value the page admits is 'a loss by reading' until §11 gives it a basis (a level the going on needs).

findings.term: a selection reaches / drains / holds itself (a noun made the doer, with its selector, its rule, its share, its winners)

examples.quote: a selection, whether a knower, a training run, a market or an optimizer, reaches only what couples into its selector, so it can meet its own criterion while what it cannot read is lost, and a rule read from its own results can hold itself there
first a map for alignment, what a selection reaches, what it can drain beyond what it reads and how its rule can lock
so an optimizer drains what lies beyond its couplings as far as any choice it has would
| selection | goes through the selector's couplings; a subset of the World premises is "a choice of premises" |

findings.states: Three dependences. (a) Which histories go on rather than others depends only on what conditions the selecting formation (its coupling closure): histories alike in what couples in go alike, so a difference that does not condition it makes no difference to what is kept. (b) Where an order rises with what couples in and there is room, the outcomes it ranks highest are those where what is not coupled in stands at its least level among the eligible outcomes. (c) Where the rule depends on the share and the share on the rule, and neither depends on anything else, the pair stays in a region the step never leaves (the grammar's not going out), whatever else changes.
findings.note: Count = 9 'a selection reaches' (overview 3, 11, 27, 57, 120 twice, 161; glossary 31, 54) + 8 'drain' + 2 'hold itself'. The centre is stated in this shape four times in full (overview 3, 11, 27; glossary 31). The glossary's row for the central word is not a definition: it presupposes a doer (the selector) and gives no relation; overview 92 defines 'a selection' as a thing that acts ('Anything that keeps, rewards, reproduces or trains toward...'), and then gives that thing a selector, which has couplings: three nested nouns for one dependence. 'Doing best' (overview 3) and 'is beaten' (118, where the glossary's row 63 says 'is exceeded') belong to the same shape. A word swap keeps it; the three sentences have to be said as dependences.

findings.term: reach, with the arrow turned round ('what a selection reaches' = what reaches it)

examples.quote: Pooling extends what a selection reaches to what some member reaches, and no further
a part acting only beyond a formation's coupling closure (all that reaches it through its couplings) is invisible to every selection through its couplings
| couples into | what reaches a selector through its couplings (never "registers") |

findings.states: In the theorem the conditions reach the selector: x couples into the selector where x is among what its step depends on. 'What a selection reaches' is that same set named from the other end, as if the selection went out to it. The relation is 缘 read one way: x conditions the selecting; the selecting depends on x.
findings.note: 9 agentive uses out of 64 forms of 'reach' in the two pages. The glossary fixes reach (及) as the transitive closure of a relation, which has a direction; the centre sentence uses it against that direction, and overview 92 uses both directions in one paragraph ('everything they reach', 'all that reaches it'). In chapter 7's use ('within a center's reach along a relation', 'a life's reach, along being affected') the relation and its direction are named each time, so those are fine. This is the knower's grammar (a gaze or hand going out to an object) laid over a dependence that runs inward.

findings.term: beyond / outside / what lies beyond (a place past the selection)

examples.quote: Whether a loss beyond a selection counts forms within becoming too
a joint selection that reads beyond its own share and does not come to select for control over its own selection
an optimum of an order rising with what couples in drains what lies beyond as far as any eligible outcome does

findings.states: What is called beyond is not apart from the selection: it depends on what the selection draws on, and the selection does not depend on it. The relation runs one way. Overview 20 says exactly this of the mussel bed: 'The bed depends on the fish and gives the fishers nothing; relations run one way ... whose death never comes back to them.' 'Reads beyond its own share' states: the rule depends on more than the share it raised.
findings.note: 44 'beyond' + 14 'outside'. By reading the lines (estimated): about 25 name a selection's or closure's outside; 5 are renewal 'from beyond/outside' a finite family (basis stated at overview 84: the family is not closed); 2+1 deny an outside to becoming ('No should stands beyond becoming'), which is the account's own claim and fine; about 10 are idiom ('beyond the model', 'beyond misreading'). Where the closure and its relation are named (overview 92 'beyond a formation's coupling closure', glossary 89 'what lies beyond it', 续无外 'nothing lies outside each center's reach along that relation') the word passes test 1. The bare forms presume separateness (test 3) where the theorem shows a one-way condition, and they hide the direction, which is the whole point. This is the shape that survived the earlier pass as 'outside'.

findings.term: read / reads / reading (no glossary row; it took over from the banned 'registers')

examples.quote: A formation depends on some conditions by threshold and reads others by level
where nothing in the loop reads beyond the share, the lock outlives a growing unread loss
with significance a free parameter that nothing else reads, a statement that reads only the dynamics
a configuration of a rule read from the share it raises in which the rule keeps favouring what it selected

findings.states: 'X reads Y' states: X's step depends on Y's level, so a difference in Y makes a difference to X (against depending by threshold, where only crossing the need does). 'A rule read from the share' states: the rule is a function of the share (overview 88 says so: 'the rule is read as a monotone function of the share'). 'Nothing in the loop reads beyond the share': nothing in the loop depends on anything but the share. 'A statement that reads only the dynamics': one whose truth depends only on the dynamics.
findings.note: 141 forms in the overview, 53 in the glossary, plus 15 'reader(s)'. Five senses under one verb, none fixed in a glossary that promises one sense each (shares estimated from the lines): (1) a formation, rule or loop reads a condition, about 40; (2) 'a rule read from the share', a passive with no reader, 9; (3) interpretation, 'read as', '[AI reading]', 'a reading', about 70, fine, since it names an interpreter and a text; (4) 'read on / in / at / across' meaning stated at, about 30, a one-for-one NAME; (5) the page's own reader, and 'readers' as members of a pool. Senses 1 and 2 put a knower facing a known where the account has a dependence; the glossary's row 52 bans 'registers' and the same grammar came back as 'reads'. Senses 1 and 2 need re-saying; sense 4 is a swap.

findings.term: winning comes to buy power over the rule that selects (with control, capture, winners)

examples.quote: the loop in which winning comes to buy power over the rule that selects
Control of the rule is not captured: where shaping the rule is selected by what comes back to the shapers
a joint selection that reads beyond its own share and does not come to select for control over its own selection

findings.states: What a rule raises comes to condition the rule: the share goes on through the rule and the rule through the share, with nothing else conditioning either, a closed loop. The pages already say it in these words: 'a loop of selection whose rule and whose reading of the rule are both formed from the share it selects' (glossary 45) and 'selected by what comes back to the shapers' (overview 161). The rule is a formation inside the loop, not something over it.
findings.note: Count: the formula 5 (overview 3, 11, 27, 88; glossary 45), 'control' 3, 'capture(d)' 10, 'winners' 1. The glossary's one sense for the account's named centre is given in a contest word (winning), a market word (buy) and a ruler's phrase (power over the rule), and the relational form comes second as its 'closed form'. The formula keeps the picture the closed form denies, a rule standing over a selection that someone can seize. 'Meta' and 'second order' (lens 7) say a level above; glossary 45 itself says 'the two are one loop' where the rule's readers are drawn from those it selects. 'Meta-attractor' is the folder's own name and can stay as a pointer to it; its defining sentence is what needs saying again.

findings.term: rule (the rule that selects, favours, raises; no glossary row)

examples.quote: A selection whose rule is read from the share it raises can hold itself.
a configuration of a rule read from the share it raises in which the rule keeps favouring what it selected
`Law` is the spine's name for a determined step, one relation (`next x = y`), not a rule its configurations obey

findings.states: The 'rule' is how the share's next step depends on kind (which kind's share does not fall), and it is itself a function of the share. It is one of the two ends of the loop, a dependence, not something that selects.
findings.note: 36 in the overview, 15 in the glossary; about 30 are the selection's rule (estimated), the rest are a test's frozen rule, an update rule, Hamilton's rule and the fishers' rule for choosing, which are fine as their fields' or the test's own terms. The word that the lock and the meta-attractor rows are built on has no row of its own, and the 'law' row defines Law by saying it is not a rule that is obeyed, while the lock row makes the rule the subject of 'favours', 'selected', 'raises' and 'reads'. A row saying what the rule is, as a dependence, would do most of the work.

findings.term: counts / has significance (said without from where); significance 'supplied', 'free'

examples.quote: Whether the loss counts.** No law of the dynamics alone says (§7).
It is supplied, the one free predicate in significance's statement
for a standpoint, a step and a formation, whether that continuation is counted from that standpoint: a proposition, not a number
from every standpoint, for anything, its continuation into the future has significance: whose losses count, every continuation's

findings.states: Significance is a three-place relation: from this standpoint, at this step, this formation's going on is counted. In the models nothing conditions it and nothing else depends on it (overview 136: 'a free parameter that nothing else reads'). On the own-closure reading it becomes a relation the root can state: the formation lies within the center's reach along a named relation.
findings.note: Count = 'whose losses count / the loss counts' 9 + 'has significance' 8. All forms of 'count' come to 76, about half arithmetic ('in counts', 'counting form') and many relational and fine ('counted from that standpoint', 'a weighting that counts each listed item above zero'). The finding is the intransitive: 'counts' and 'has significance' say a relation as a property and drop the standpoint (test 4). This is a true slot: the glossary defines significance by 'counted' and 'counted' by nothing, and the overview says so plainly ('supplied', 7; 'free', 17). A new name would hide the hole. What can change is to keep 'from which standpoint' in the sentence wherever 'counts' appears, and to keep overview 136's sentence that the non-entailment is by construction and does not show that becoming leaves significance undetermined.

findings.term: the dynamics | the ethics (scope, order, significance): 'the dynamics leave it free', 'do not settle it'

examples.quote: the theorems, drawn on the dynamics alone, do not settle it, and the ethics emerges from continuation
How courses rank: no law of the dynamics ranks.
Nothing in the represented dynamics, which leave scope and order free by construction (§7)

findings.states: In the models, the step does not depend on the significance parameter or on the order, and neither depends on the step: the fact and value distinction is drawn here as the independence of two parameters of a model. What the account holds of becoming is the other thing: standards and orders form, are conditioned and condition ('real in what they condition', overview 134), and that line is not yet in the models (overview 142, 204: the open target).
findings.note: 'dynamics' 21 + 3; 'represented dynamics' 6; 'by construction' 9; 'leave(s) ... free/open' 9. The basis of the distinction is stated (a modelling choice, by construction), so it passes test 1 where 'represented' and 'by construction' are present. Where they are dropped ('No law of the dynamics alone says', 'What the dynamics leave open' as a heading) 'the dynamics' reads as a domain of fact with an actor's verbs (says, ranks, leaves, forces) and the ethics as a second domain beside it. Keep 'represented' and 'by construction' with every use; the short forms are where the two-kinds reading enters.

findings.term: loss / lost (an ending or a fall named from a standpoint that is not said)

examples.quote: a course once locked stays locked whatever loss nothing in it reads
a selection, whether a knower, a training run, a market or an optimizer, reaches only what couples into its selector, so it can meet its own criterion while what it cannot read is lost
the lock outliving a growing unread coordinate

findings.states: In the lock theorem: a coordinate nothing in the loop depends on grows, and the loop goes on unchanged. In the World: a level falls, or a formation stops going on, while the criterion that couples in is met. It is a loss from the standpoint of what ends or of what depended on it.
findings.note: 55 'loss(es)', plus 3 'lost' and 5 'lose(s)'. The overview's own table already has the plain form ('a growing unread coordinate', 183). Calling it a loss counts it before the sentence asks whether it counts: 'Whether a loss beyond a selection counts forms within becoming too' (3). Where the bearer is named the word is fine and should stay ('every continuation's loss', 'who bears the bed's end', 'the losses of those who depend on one'). In the statements of the theorems, 'what ends' or 'what falls' says what is proved; 'loss' belongs where a standpoint is given.

findings.term: own / self / self-concern (a marking supplied; 'how a self is drawn' not fixed)

examples.quote: what is one's own is a region drawn along a relation no law of the dynamics fixes
an order increasing in its own continuation, which the order's marking marks
concern for another need not make the other one's own

findings.states: 'Own' is a region closed under a named relation: on the own-closure reading, what lies within a center's reach along it; in the Lean, a marking the order is given (AddsOwn). Self and other are then two sides of a boundary drawn along that relation, and which relation draws it is not derived.
findings.note: 'own' 44 + 18; 'self' 36 + 16, of which 'self-concern(ed)' 27 + 15. Chapter 7's passages say the basis and say it is open ('a region drawn along a relation', 'a proposal about what one's own is', 'no law singles that class out'), so the slot is marked, and the glossary's boundary row (23) gives inside and outside by a region closed under a relation. Two things remain. The name 'self-concern' presents a self with its concern as known, against others, while its definition's reach holds 'what sustains it and what draws on the same conditions alike'; and the glossary admits two senses for it (the order, and a scope), against its one-sense promise. In the centre sentence 'its own share / winners / criterion / results' (about 20) is only the reflexive of a loop, what it itself raised, and is fine: it says a coming back.

findings.term: emerges (the ethics emerges from continuation)

examples.quote: "Emerges" names neither a derivation nor a shown development
the theorems, drawn on the dynamics alone, do not settle it, and the ethics emerges from continuation

findings.states: Orders and scopes are formations: they come about through lives going on and through what conditions those lives, and they condition what comes after. How they form, spread and lock is not shown; what is shown is conditional on the continuation condition and self-concern as hypotheses.
findings.note: 5 in the overview, 1 in the glossary. The word marks a place the account takes as wanted and not derived, and overview 142 says so in full. It is used four times before that scoping (3, 27, glossary 69, overview 142's own opening), so a reader of the top paragraph meets it as a claim. It also carries a level picture (something rising out of a base). Keep the slot visible: say 'forms within' with 'how is open' beside it, as 142 does.

findings.term: forbids / Forbids / a theorem's verdict (theses and theorems as legislators)

examples.quote: The root's theorems hold of every relation and so forbid none
It forbids an explanation needing what no relation carries, such as an intrinsic value
where a theorem's verdict holds

findings.states: A thesis and the named case do not hold together: if the case is observed, the thesis is wrong. A theorem 'forbids' a case where no model of its hypotheses has it. Both are relations between a statement and what it holds of.
findings.note: 'forbid(s)/forbidden' 16 + 1 (a column head in two tables); 'verdict' 8 + 1. 'Forbids' is the falsificationist's term and is fine as the theses' column head if it is said once whose term it is. Used of the account's own theorems it is the same picture 'law' carried, which the glossary's new theorem row (98) sets aside: 'is read off what it holds of and not set over it'. For theorems, 'excludes' or 'no model of its hypotheses has' says it one for one; 'a theorem's verdict' (glossary 23) is 'a theorem's conclusion'. A test's frozen verdict and 'a way of seeing, not a verdict' are fine. 'Must' (6) and 'requirement' (16) are mostly conditional need ('a coupled member must act on the loss') and are not findings; 'the condition's asking', 'C asks' personify a hypothesis, locally.

findings.term: law of the dynamics (says, ranks, fixes, gives, singles out) and the declared residue 'shared law', 'first law'

examples.quote: Whether the loss counts.** No law of the dynamics alone says (§7).
No law of the dynamics gives one: the theorems give how courses differ in what they admit
"Shared law" keeps the earlier word for a theorem until the names are revised

findings.states: No statement that depends only on the represented dynamics entails the continuation condition or a ranking (the theorem is named at overview 157, ReadsOnlyDynamics.not_entails). 'No law fixes the boundary': no theorem of the account singles out the relation along which a self is drawn.
findings.note: Six uses where a 'law' is the subject of saying, ranking, fixing or giving (overview 20, 63, 153 twice, 155; glossary 72); these were missed by the change to 'theorem' on 13 November and are one-for-one. 'Law' in all is 39 + 20. About 17 in the overview are the determined step (giving law, one law of four parts, law of exchange, 'acting by its own law'), which glossary 99 defines as one relation and which are fine; 5 are sciences' or the corpus's own laws, fine as pointers; 'the five shared laws' and the glossary's 'first law' and 'shared law' rows keep the old word for a theorem, declared as pending.

findings.term: correspondence / faithful representation / actual systems (the model here, the world there)

examples.quote: That actual systems meet these premises is open, a correspondence not shown.
That any of this reaches actual fisheries or AI is a correspondence, not shown.
that every becoming has a faithful representation in the grammar is open

findings.states: Whether an actual fishery or training run is one of the things the theorem holds of, that is, whether it meets the premises and so falls in the class, is not shown. 'Meet these premises' already says it.
findings.note: 'correspondence' 10, 'actual' 19, 'faithful representation' 2, 'represent-' 15 + 3. The scoping is right and has to stay at full strength. The word says it as two realms matched one to one, which is the picture overview 92 sets aside for knowing ('not a mirror beside it'), and the account has its own word for a model (a lumping, 理). Where the sentence already has 'meets the premises', 'a correspondence' adds only the mirror. 'Representation' in the technical sense (the World represented in the grammar both ways, checked in Lean) is a stated mapping and fine.

findings.term: occurrence / carrier / relatum (what relations are between; no glossary row)

examples.quote: | relation (际, *jì*) | a two-place predicate on a carrier, the one kind of symbol |
every theorem holds for every carrier and relation, so no kind of thing is chosen first
there is one unfolding, and whatever is, is how it relates within it

findings.states: The grammar takes a carrier (any type of occurrences) and a relation on it; the theorems hold for every carrier, so none is privileged, but a carrier is given before its relation. That an occurrence is nothing before how it relates is the philosophical thesis, argued and not proved.
findings.note: 'occurrence(s)' 4 + 6, 'carrier(s)' 4 + 6; 'relatum/relata' 7 + 4 besides. The root rows of the glossary define relation, class, the marks and continuation over 'occurrences' and 'a carrier', and neither word has a row. The formal shape (a type first, a predicate on it) is the one place where the account's own form puts something before its conditions; overview 68 handles it honestly ('no kind of thing is chosen first'). A row for 'occurrence' that says this, and points to the thesis as argued, would show the slot; a new name would hide it.

findings.term: install / installed (a scope or a law put into a learner)

examples.quote: training installs a law only along the learner's own courses, and off them only where the lumping it reads through cannot tell a history from a course
The scope can be installed, and it carries

findings.states: What a learner does after training is fixed along the courses the training went through, and elsewhere only where a history is lumped with one of them. T4: fishers told of the bed, the scope and the rule keep the bed in more seasons, and (untested) go on doing so in a new setting.
findings.note: Overview 21 (heading), 96, 161, 180 and link text. An installer, a thing installed and a container; 'it carries' makes the scope an object moved. The theorem's own sentence, once 'installs' is taken out, is already a dependence. Overview 96 uses 'installation' for what the model does not represent, which is fine.

findings.term: how far it has been seen (a claim seen, with no one seeing)

examples.quote: Each claim says how far it has been seen, in these words
what kind of claim a statement is and how far it has been seen, as its label says: definition, theorem with its base, conditional, calibration, thesis, assessment, reading, open

findings.states: By what a claim is held: a proof (on which base), a test (frozen, and how it came out), an argument, a reading (whose), or nothing yet. A relation between a statement and its check.
findings.note: 3 in the overview (two are column heads), 4 in the glossary. Mild: the labels themselves name the relation, and the phrase is the project's own, so this may be left. It is listed because it replaced 'standing' on 9 November with another figure of the same kind, sight without a seer; 'what it rests on' would say the relation. T6's 'A break is seen coming only through what couples into what breaks' is the opposite case and good: seeing said as a dependence.

findings.term: the proxy problem ... what a proxy does not register; blindness; invisible

examples.quote: It is the proxy problem in its blindness to what a proxy does not register

findings.states: The theorem is the field's proxy problem in one of its forms: a measure does not depend on what does not couple into it. 'Invisible to every selection through its couplings' states: makes no difference to any of them.
findings.note: The field's term, named as the field's, so fine as a pointer; 'proxy' 3 times, each attributed. But 'register' is the one word the glossary (52) says is never used, and it is used here in the account's own gloss; 'couple in' is the fixed word. 'Blindness' and 'invisible' (3) are the knower's words for the same dependence and are local.

findings.term: aligned with ... within the whole (the direction offered to AI)

examples.quote: The direction we offer AI is AI formation, learning, action and revision aligned with actual living and further generation within the whole.
Alignment is first a question with no premise: what a selection can reach.

findings.states: Offered, by the authors: that what forms AI, and what AI learns, does and revises, depend on (couple into) what lives and what can still form, so that an ending there can turn the course. The second sentence already recasts the field's word as a question about dependence.
findings.note: 'align-' 17 + 1, nearly all the field's word used as a pointer and fine. The finding is the one sentence: two things with one brought into line with the other, 'the whole' with no relation saying which whole (the glossary gives 'the whole' a sense only as a closure along a relation), and 'generation' used outside the glossary's fixed sense ('never means arising, nor any new organization'). It is marked as offered and by whom, which passes test 4. 'Keeps humans and AI ... out of instrumental convergence and the meta-attractor' is a container figure; local.

findings.term: 无明: 'seeking locked onto a target' (purpose words inside a definition)

examples.quote: seeking locked onto a target that cannot be met at rest, grounded in, and not the same as, the position every formation selects from

findings.states: Not recoverable from the row: it should say which dependence is meant (presumably a selection whose criterion no state at rest meets, so that it never comes to rest), in the words of the home section. I did not read chapter 03, so this is a question for its reader.
findings.note: The traditional terms are pointers and fine. The gloss defines them with a seeker, a target and a position, and as a definition it does not say a relation; the second half ('coupling joined to a selection so that it reaches what support does not mark') is nearer one.

kept: Both pages already say many relations well, and these should be kept as they are. The root section of the overview (lines 68-78) is written almost wholly in the root's words: 'x is among what y's coming about comes from', 'a class, a sameness in some respect', 'the wood ends, the fire goes on', and 'relata of one kind (formations where they take and give, conditions where they are drawn on)'; the glossary's formation row (35) gives formation and condition as two roles of one relatum. Overview 54 states two pairs as one relation each: 'taker and drawn-on, two roles of one relatum; knower and known, one reading loop'. Overview 92: 'Knowing is a relation within the unfolding, not a mirror beside it', with couplings that 'belong to the same web as everything they reach'. Overview 98 puts the agent's verbs inside one determined step: 'senses, predicts, chooses, acts and revises as one law of four parts'. Overview 20 says the centre as a one-way relation and is the model for re-saying 'beyond': 'The bed depends on the fish and gives the fishers nothing; relations run one way ... whose death never comes back to them.' The closed form of the meta-attractor is already relational: 'a loop of selection whose rule and whose reading of the rule are both formed from the share it selects' (glossary 45), 'selected by what comes back to the shapers' (overview 161). Generation, keeping and degeneration are given as three cases on branches at two grains, with 'Degeneration belongs to the unfolding as fully as generation, and 02's map orders nothing' (82). Widening is 'a relation between two courses' with three cases, 'more and less future ... not good and evil', and 'a judgment that settles one names its criterion and who holds it' (140); the glossary's ranking row says 'a relation formed by whoever compares' (72): test 4 met. The glossary's boundary row (23) gives inside and outside by a region closed under a relation; its theorem row (98) says 'read off what it holds of and not set over it', and its law row (99) 'one relation, not a rule its configurations obey'. Overview 165: 'Distinctions such as fact and value are drawn along relations, with what they leave out. Nonduality is a requirement of method.' Overview 136 keeps the slot honest: non-entailment 'by construction, not that becoming leaves significance undetermined'. 'Couples into', 'depends on' (60 uses), 'goes on' (28), 'comes back' and 'giving waits on giving' (122, in place of cooperation and defection) are the pages' working relation words. The field terms (proxy problem, tragedy of the commons, instrumental convergence, deceptive alignment, Price, Fisher, Hamilton, Sen, Pareto) are each named as the field's and used as pointers. The denials of an outside ('No should stands beyond becoming', 续无外 with its relation named) and 'within becoming' (22 uses), paired with 'real in what they condition' (134), are the account's own claim and fine. Not found in either page: entity, mechanism, nature, information about, signal, govern, constraint, principal and agent.
top_three: The centre sentence's shape, in both pages: 'a selection reaches ... drains beyond what it reads ... its rule locks' (overview 3, 11, 27; glossary 31), with 'beyond / outside' as its place (58 uses). It makes a noun the doer, turns the arrow of 'reach' round, and names as an outside what the theorems show as a one-way condition: what is 'beyond' depends on what the selection draws on, and the selection does not depend on it. Overview 20 already says it that way. It needs re-saying as three dependences; a word swap keeps it, as 'outside' did.

'read / reads / reading': 194 forms, five senses, no glossary row, and the direct heir of the banned 'registers'. Where a formation, a rule or a loop 'reads', the sentence states a dependence (its step differs with that level; the rule is a function of the share), and 'a rule read from the share' is a passive with no reader. The interpretive sense ('read as', '[AI reading]') is fine and should be the one sense the word keeps.

'counts / has significance' said without from where, with significance 'supplied' and 'free' and 'the dynamics' set beside 'the ethics': a real slot, honestly marked, where fact and value are two independent parameters of the models. It should stay visible (keep 'from which standpoint', 'represented', 'by construction'), not be renamed. Close behind: the glossary's defining sentence for the meta-attractor, 'winning comes to buy power over the rule that selects', which states the account's named centre in contest, market and ruler words while its own closed form says a loop.

findings.term: the centre sentence: a selection (or 'what picks among things by a rule') reads, lowers what lies beyond, locks on what it selected

examples.quote: of any selection (a reward, a judge, a market, a vote, a training run) it asks what the selection reads or needs, what lies beyond that, whether it can do better on what it reads by lowering what lies beyond, and whether its rule can lock on what it already selected
a joint selection that reads beyond its own share and does not come to select for control over its own selection

what picks among things by a rule (a reward, a judge, a market, a training run) can use up what the rule does not count, can lock itself in where the rule is updated from its own picks, and in built examples loses what would have read the loss

findings.states: Among lines that go on, how much each goes on next (its share) depends on a score. The score depends on only some of what those lines go on through. So a share can rise while the level of something the lines, or others, depend on falls, and the score stays the same. Where the next score is set from the present shares, the same share comes back at every renewal. There is no selector and no 'beyond': there are two dependences, one that the score also depends on and one that it does not.
findings.note: Five sentences state the centre this way (MAP.md:9 twice, THE-MAP.md:11, and the path opener at THE-MAP.md:23 = PATHS.md:14); hand count. Word counts by grep: select* 13 in MAP.md; pick* 21 in THE-MAP, 46 in PATHS; 'beyond' 4 in MAP.md (3 in this sentence), 4 in PATHS. THE-MAP.md:11 is the 12 November rewording of MAP.md:9: 'selection' became 'what picks', 'beyond' became 'what the rule does not count', and the doer, the thing done to and the reflexive ('lock itself in') all stayed. MAP.md:9 still carries the older wording whole.

findings.term: 'the rule' as grammatical subject: the rule favours, picks, leaves out, scores, counts, uses up, turns

examples.quote: Where a rule leaves something out and that thing is being used up, the rule scores the outcome the same however much is used; what lives on that thing bears it.
a rule that still counts what it uses up, set with the rest counting too, and a choosing in which shaping the rule does not pay
No theorem says what first makes a rule start to be updated from its own picks.

findings.states: 'The rule' is how each side's next share depends on a score (a reward, a price, a count of votes). 'The rule favours X' says X's share is larger at the next step. 'The rule leaves X out' says the score does not change when the level of X changes. 'Updated from its own picks' says the next score depends on the present shares. 'The rule turns' says the larger share passes to the other side.
findings.note: 27 is 'the rule' directly followed by an acting verb (14 in THE-MAP, 13 in PATHS, by a grep pattern, so a lower bound). 'the rule' in all: 41 in THE-MAP, 53 in PATHS, 1 in MAP.md. The cast's definition is relational and can stay ('the rule: what the picking goes by', THE-MAP.md:29; 'what sets the rule: those the rule is set from', :36). The split enters when that dependence is made a box-like thing that acts, with a 'who sets it' behind it and a 'what it leaves out' in front of it. PATHS.md:85 also shows a slot: what brings a score to depend on its own shares is not derived.

findings.term: 'given from outside' against 'of the course itself'; unconditioned starters ('something gives without waiting')

examples.quote: Every other way out drawn needs something given from outside, or is shown only in a built example or as a reading.
Once nothing is given, giving comes back only if something gives without waiting.
Telling them apart needs a trial that treats them differently, brought in from beyond what it has.

findings.states: The theorem assumes a further premise and does not derive it: the step depends on a condition whose own conditions are not among the ties drawn. The page's gloss already says so: 'proved only with a further premise put in, which the step names ... Which premises are marked as given from outside is the map's own marking, not a difference between two kinds of proof' (THE-MAP.md:38).
findings.note: 'given from outside': 13 in THE-MAP, 43 in PATHS; 39 of them are the step and arrow marker (6 + 33). 'of the course itself': 5 + 5. Variants in PATHS (13): 'something gives without waiting', 'starts carrying it without being handed it', 'something outside the group gives', 'brought in from beyond', plus the box 'Set from outside'. The hole is real and honestly marked, so it is a slot. What the word adds is a place: the course becomes a container with an inside, and the missing condition becomes a thing arriving from an outside, or a thing that starts with no conditions, which the root denies. A new wording keeps the hole visible only if it still says 'a premise assumed, not derived, named here'. The headline tally at THE-MAP.md:107 ('14 need something given from outside') rests on this marking.

findings.term: reflexive self-action: holds itself in place, lock itself in, closed on itself, its own picks, its own checks

examples.quote: ## The first path: A rule that holds itself in place
Where the judging of the rule is set by that same side too, the lock is closed on itself.
The loop reaches its own checks: the ways a loss could come to count are filled from inside and, one order further, breaking them is what gets rewarded.

findings.states: A ring of dependence: the next score depends on the shares the last score gave, so the same share comes back at each renewal. Where the judgments that could change the score also depend on those shares, nothing else makes a difference to it. Two sentences in these pages already say a ring without a self: 'people learn it because machines have it, and machines have it because people learned it' (THE-MAP.md:48) and 'A line closes into a ring at exactly the step where something then acting responds to a level that lies downstream of what it gives to' (PATHS.md:297).
findings.note: 33 = grep for lock(s|ed) itself/on/in, holds itself, closed on itself, carries itself, growing on itself (1 MAP.md, 9 THE-MAP, 23 PATHS). 'its own': 6 + 13 + 34. 'inside': 5 + 16, including 'anything inside it', 'filled from inside', 'nothing inside the view', 'nothing inside moves it on'. The reflexive makes a self that acts on itself and an inside it closes; this is the title of the first path and the name of a box ('Holds itself in place', 'Judged only by its own picks', 'Even the checks are its own'). 'One order further' (2) adds a level above in the same sentence, in a step marked as a reading.

findings.term: yes-or-no boxes: a row 'asks', a box is 'one way the answer can stand', a boundary is a question

[Shaping the rule costs](PLACES.md#box-bs-costs) | [Shaping the rule pays](PLACES.md#box-bs-pays): does the return to shapers alone cover the cost? *(a proved boundary)*

Each fish left in the bay also counts, a seventh as much as one caught. At [The cost counts](PLACES.md#box-b2-counted), set up so; found instead at [Using up what is not counted](PLACES.md#box-b2-uncounted).

findings.states: Each row is one relation with an amount: how much of what is spared comes back to the one that spared it; how much difference the level of a thing makes to the score, against how much a catch makes; what comes back to the shapers against what they spent. The boxes are the two sides of a line on that one relation. PATHS.md:122 says it as a relation: 'does what one alone spares come back to it more than one for one?'
findings.note: 14 = the marker '(a proved boundary)' (1 in THE-MAP, 13 in PATHS); 10 of the PATHS ones are worded as yes-or-no questions; 12 distinct box pairs. Pairs said as two things: 'Shaping the rule costs / pays', 'The cost counts / Using up what is not counted', 'Nothing it does comes back / What it does comes back', 'Has what it needs / Short of what it needs', 'Set from outside / Follows its own picks'. The tests show the cost of the form: 'pairing' occurs 5 + 12 times, and the pairing gave way or was in doubt in 5 of the 7 tests. In LA4 a bay counted 'a seventh as much' was placed at 'The cost counts' and found at 'not counted'; in LA1b a bonus raised from 2 to 32 was placed at 'The cost counts' and changed nothing (PATHS.md:505); in IN1 'told to count it' was placed there and the bed was kept 1 season in 10. 'Counts' is a degree along one relation, and the box made it a yes.

findings.term: 'a view' against 'the thing itself' and 'how things are'

examples.quote: each is a view of something, and what comes back from that thing can correct it or fail to
A view is checked when it has just been set beside the thing itself, where it could have come out otherwise; it fits as of that look.
While each change is recorded as the kind it is and the reports fit, how things actually are stays among those held possible.

findings.states: What something does next depends on a record of what came back from its earlier acts. The record changes only through what comes back from further acts. Two states are alike for it exactly as long as they give alike returns to the acts it takes, which PATHS.md:203 says: 'they look alike exactly as long as they answer alike the acts it actually takes'. 'Fits' means that what the record leads it to expect and what comes back are alike over those acts.
findings.note: 66 = 'view' 45 (7 THE-MAP, 38 PATHS) + 'the thing itself' 13 (1 + 12) + 'how things are/were/actually are' 8 (3 + 5). This pair frames the whole third path and a band title ('A view and how things are', THE-MAP.md:124). 'The thing itself' names a thing apart from every meeting with it, set against a picture held by 'whatever holds the view'; the theorems are about records, answers and acts, and need neither. 'Nothing inside the view shows the difference' (PATHS.md:184) adds an inside. In the path's own steps the relation is mostly already said ('each answer can only remove', 'the record fixes what an act does there exactly when it has been taken there'); the pair is in the names of the row, the boxes and the opener.

findings.term: placing a thing in a box; an arrow as 'a way from one box to another' with the condition as its tag

examples.quote: To place a thing, find on each row that applies to it the box that fits it; the boxes drawn so far need not hold every answer.
An arrow with a head is a way from one box to another: along a row, a change of that row's answer; between rows, from one row's answer to another's.
Each test is laid on the map with what in it was taken as which box, what the reasoning said, what was seen and what gave way.

findings.states: A box is a class: what goes alike under one stated condition. An arrow is a theorem: under a named condition, what is in one class at a step is in another at a later step. The condition is what the theorem states; the drawing makes the classes the nodes and the condition a caption on the line between them.
findings.note: 62 = arrows written with '→' in PATHS; the sheet has 50 boxes, 105 arrows, 14 rows (THE-MAP.md:13, :148). The word 'box' is visible 25 times in THE-MAP. The form names a thing first and then gives it places, one per row, as if the places were its properties; the tests then record 'set up so' (22) and 'found so / found instead at' (11), a thing moved from one box to another. Rows that 'apply to it' and the band 'Of anything that keeps going' do state a respect. The path names are already relations ('Living on what comes back', 'Giving that waits on giving', 'What each turn brings back'); the box names are mostly states of a thing ('Has what it needs', 'Ended').

findings.term: reads, counts, tells, sees, shows the loss; 'what would have read the loss'

examples.quote: the loss gets back to it in time exactly where at least one of them can tell it while what is being lost can still be kept
no rule that goes only by whether those things keep going can read it in time
In built examples, what is used up is what the readers of the loss stood on. They are removed.

findings.states: The loss makes a difference to a judgment from which the score is set. 'In time' says: while the level is still where it can come back. The cast defines it this way once and well: 'what reads the loss, or counts it: anything among what sets the rule whose judgment changes with the loss' (THE-MAP.md:35).
findings.note: Estimated: about 60 uses in this sense. By grep, read* occurs 45 times in THE-MAP and 73 in PATHS (these include 'AI readers' and 'a reading', which are fine: they say whose reading), count* 32 and 109; can/cannot tell, read, see and looks alike 5 and 31. After the definition the steps use read, count, tell, note, carry, see and show for the one relation, and the perceiving words bring back a knower facing a known ('readers of the loss', 'counters of the loss'). 'Makes a difference to' is already used three times in each page and would replace most of them one for one. Fine where it is the test's own setting: a judge model that reads nine answers, fishers told of a bed.

findings.term: pays, cost, the loss, bears; the favoured side, its lead, outweigh, outvoted

examples.quote: Shaping the rule in the shapers' own favour pays wherever what comes back to the shapers alone covers the cost.
**the loss**: how much has been used up of something the rule leaves out. What lives on that thing bears it. It is still called the loss once something counts it.
a calculation beforehand marked five open (holding back pays) and six locked (against others who pick at every step, holding back gains a picker next to nothing)

findings.states: 'Pays' says that what comes back to the one that gave is more than it gave. 'The loss' says how far the level of something has fallen that the score does not depend on, and that what lives on it goes on less. 'The lead' is the favoured share told as a distance from the others.
findings.note: 79 = pays/pay/paid 51 (13 + 38) + cost 28 (7 + 21). 'the loss' 29 + 43; favour* 21 + 25. 'Pays' is a market name for a return, and the box 'What it spares comes back to it' already says the same thing in the root's words, so this is one for one. 'The loss' has its basis stated once (lost to what lives on it, left out by the rule), which meets the fourth test; it then stands as a bare noun 72 times. 'Cost' has two senses on one page: what the shapers spend (THE-MAP.md:56) and the loss itself (box 'The cost counts'). 'Best' (7 + 47) is nearly always indexed ('the best by the rule', 'the best catch for the three'), which is the comparison said, and is kept.

findings.term: use up, removed, 'the lead used up', 'the shapers: what spends to change the rule in its own favour'

examples.quote: In one built example the rule had turned; but the lead, grown large, used up what the counters of the loss stood on. They were gone, and the lock came back for good.
built case: the lead removed what counted the loss
**the shapers**: what spends to change the rule in its own favour.

findings.states: As the favoured share grows, more is taken from a level; what made the loss count went on through that level; when the level is gone, it ends. For the shapers: some of what is picked gives up something, the next score then gives them a larger share, and what comes back to them is more than they gave.
findings.note: 41 = use up/used up/using up 34 (10 + 24) + remov* 7 (2 + 5). 'The lead' and 'the rule' are nouns made into doers, and 'They are removed' implies a remover where the theorem has a dependence ('stood on'). The passive 'is being used up' (THE-MAP.md:47) and 'what lives on that thing bears it' are closer to what is stated. 'Shapers' with 'its own favour' (4) gives an interest to a party before the tie that returns to it is said; the second half of THE-MAP.md:56 says the tie.

findings.term: 'law' for the account's proved statements, and 'follows a fixed law'

examples.quote: No law in it evaluates: there is no should beyond becoming and no good and evil set over it
The core's source declarations have empty axiom reports, so each law holds constructively
Where the thing follows a fixed law through finitely many states

findings.states: In MAP.md: a theorem, a statement proved under named premises. In PATHS: the same state is always followed by the same next one, which PATHS.md:321 says in exactly those words.
findings.note: 6 in MAP.md (lines 9 and 11) for the account's own statements, beside 'theorem' in the same paragraph ('a **theorem** ... a **calibration**, where a law needs an omniscience principle'); 2 in PATHS (177, 221) for a thing that 'follows' a law. Not findings: 'Goodhart's law' (2 in THE-MAP, 1 in PATHS), a pointer; and the link text 'what the theorems say' already reads theorem, though its target file is LAWS.md (THE-MAP.md:159). MAP.md:9 denies a should 'beyond' and a good 'set over': the denial is the theory's own and stays; it is worded in the spatial terms it denies.

findings.term: 'has significance', 'whose losses count', 'self-concern ... its own continuation ... within its reach', 'ranks above'

examples.quote: the continuation condition (from every standpoint, for anything, its continuation into the future has significance), which fixes whose losses count and alone ranks nothing
self-concern, an order ranking above what it widens every widening that adds to its own continuation, read as what lies within its reach
That a life forms such an order is not shown: in the proofs it is a hypothesis, and how scope and order form is the work's open target

findings.states: The theorems that compare courses take an order as a hypothesis and say what follows under it. How an order, and the range of what it is affected by, forms in a life going on through what sustains it is not derived. MAP.md says this itself in the third quote.
findings.note: 14 = rank* 7 + significance 7 in MAP.md (three of the latter are the chapter's name in links). 'Has significance' is a possession with no relation given; 'self', 'its own' and 'within its reach' presume a bounded self whose reach is then widened. The page marks it as a hypothesis and as open, so a better name would hide a hole; what can change is saying it as 'taken as a premise'. The hinge sentence does state a relation: 'where relations of being affected close'.

findings.term: 'Where the reasoning met the world'; 'What the reasoning said' against 'What was seen'; 'whether the representation fits the world'

examples.quote: ## Where the reasoning met the world
**What the reasoning said.** Untold, the bed lies beyond what their choosing reads, so it will not be kept.
what a passing run does not show (whether the premises hold, whether the readings fit, whether the representation fits the world)

findings.states: A forecast was written and fixed before a run; the run's record was set beside it; where they differ, one tie between them gave way: a theorem's condition, the pairing of the case with a box, or the measure. THE-MAP.md:93 says this in its first sentence.
findings.note: 21 = the heading (1) + the 'What the reasoning said' and 'What was seen' labels (2 in THE-MAP, 16 in PATHS) + 2 'the world' in MAP.md. 'the reasoning' in all: 8 + 44. The heading sets reasoning on one side and a world on the other. Each test's last block does the opposite and is kept: 'Where this left the account's own view' places the account on its own row of the map, a view corrected or not by what came back. Six of the seven tests ran in built set-ups, which the page says; 'the world' overstates that as well.

findings.term: 'the ways out', 'the ways back', 'another way in', 'where it is too late'

examples.quote: **The ways out**

One way out is proved of the course itself: where the loss gets back to the rule in time, the rest count it, and the judgments together go against what the rule favoured at two updates running, the rule turns.
A box outlined in green dashes is one the work wants to reach.

findings.states: Conditions under which the favoured share stops coming back at each renewal ('the rule turns'), and conditions under which a level that fell comes back. That these are wanted is the work's own wanting, which the page says outright: 'This is wanted; it is not shown' (THE-MAP.md:80).
findings.note: 20 = way(s) out/back/in/down (7 + 13). 'Out' and 'in' make the lock an enclosure and carry a direction of better without saying it there. The page does say the comparison and from where in two places, which meets the fourth test and is kept: the green boxes are 'what the work wants', and 'That order is ours: an order of open and closed, not of better and worse' (THE-MAP.md:107). 'Too late' (1 + 4) has its basis stated ('while what is being lost can still be kept') and is fine.

findings.term: 'allowed', 'lowest allowed level', 'the rest of the process allows it', 'an instruction governed a step'

examples.quote: Or only outcomes that keep every need are allowed. Then the best by the rule takes only the spare.
every best outcome by the rule leaves the uncounted thing at its lowest allowed level
Where an instruction governed a step, the commit message quotes it.

findings.states: The outcomes compared are only those in which every need is met: a premise on the set of outcomes, which the step marks as assumed. 'Lowest allowed level' is the lowest level among the outcomes compared. In MAP.md:40: where a step followed an instruction.
findings.note: allow* 1 + 2 + 10. 'Allowed' implies something that permits, where the theorem has a restricted set of outcomes. Local. 'Complies', 'checked' and 'the verdict' in the TR7A test are that game's own terms and are fine there; 'judge' for a language model that scores answers is the field's term.

findings.term: other fields' names: Goodhart's law, regulatory capture, instrumental convergence, the meta-attractor, the earlier folders' one-liners

examples.quote: Close to what others call: [Goodhart's law, in its popular wording](PLACES.md#box-b2-uncounted); [cumulative advantage (the Matthew effect in its generalised form)](PLACES.md#box-b1-held); [regulatory capture](PLACES.md#box-bs-pays)
out of instrumental convergence and the meta-attractor
Selection on axes where winning buys capacity to win remakes the minds it scores

findings.states: Each name points at what another field or an earlier folder described; the map says a place is close to it, within limits its reading states.
findings.note: 45 is the page's own figure for names others gave (THE-MAP.md:154), not a grep count. On the map pages they are attributed ('Close to what others call') and limited ('it is not the source's agreement', THE-MAP.md:157): fine. In MAP.md two are not marked as pointers. 'Instrumental convergence' (1) is the AI-safety field's term used as the account's own. The table 'The earlier theory folders' gives each folder 'in one line' in doer, contest and market words ('winning buys capacity to win', 'competition that selects survivors hands winners the rule', 'Technology amplifies the operating logic it runs under', 'Actors act from narrative-value frames'); these are the folders' own claims, not live, and are fine if the column says 'in its own words'. 'Meta-attractor' (4 + 1 + 1) is the account's name, given as a name at THE-MAP.md:52 ('The account calls this loop the meta-attractor'); 'meta' suggests a level above where the step states a ring. 'The selection mechanism' (MAP.md:36) is one local use of 'mechanism'.

kept: Much of these pages already says relations, most of it in the steps and less in the names and headings. The path titles are relations: 'Living on what comes back', 'Giving that waits on giving', 'What each turn brings back'. The fourth and fifth paths are nearly free of doer and beyond: 'Each gives because what it waits on gave, so the giving carries on' (PATHS.md:237), 'A pattern can go on while what carries it is replaced' (:265), 'A line closes into a ring at exactly the step where something then acting responds to a level that lies downstream of what it gives to' (:297), 'A difference going round gets smaller only through a link that passes on less than it got' (:304). 'Comes back / gets back' occurs 24 + 74 times and 'depends on, waits on, lives on, stands on, rests on' 15 + 34: these are the root's words and carry the pages. The cast defines several words by a relation: 'what reads the loss, or counts it: anything ... whose judgment changes with the loss'; 'what sets the rule: those the rule is set from'; 'its lead is the same thing told as how far ahead of the rest it is' (one relation, two tellings). 'Best' is indexed ('the best by the rule', 'the best catch for the three'). The comparison and its standpoint are said where the map orders or wants: 'That order is ours: an order of open and closed, not of better and worse ... a count on an order we chose, not a finding' (THE-MAP.md:107) and 'This is wanted; it is not shown' (:80). The marking of how far each step is seen (proved, with a premise assumed, a built example, a reading) is kept, with the gloss that it is 'the map's own marking, not a difference between two kinds of proof'. Boundaries say 'what a thing turns on and show nothing moving' (PATHS.md:222), and each path ends by saying what no theorem derives. Other fields' names are attributed and limited. Each test ends by placing the account's own view on the map's own row, so the account stands in the same net as what it describes. In MAP.md: 'its ethics emerges from continuation, from a life going on through what sustains it' and 'where relations of being affected close'.
top_three: The centre is still said with a doer, a thing done to and a place outside it, and 'the rule' is the doer's new name. MAP.md:9 keeps the old sentence whole ('what the selection reads ... lowering what lies beyond ... lock on what it already selected ... control over its own selection'); THE-MAP.md:11 replaced the words and kept the grammar ('what picks among things by a rule can use up what the rule does not count, can lock itself in'). 'The rule' then acts 27 times and 'itself / its own' names the first path. What is stated is a ring of dependence: shares depend on a score, the score on only some of what the shares go on through, and the next score on the present shares. The pages already say such a ring without a self at THE-MAP.md:48 (the keyboard) and PATHS.md:297.

The form of the sheet says one relation as two things. A row 'asks', a box is 'one way the answer can stand', 10 boundaries are yes-or-no questions, and a thing is 'placed' in a box. Each row is one relation with an amount (how much comes back to the one that spared; how much difference a level makes to the score). The tests show what the cut costs: the pairing of a case with a box gave way or was in doubt in 5 of 7 tests, and in three the case was placed at 'The cost counts' when the level counted only a little ('a seventh as much', PATHS.md:447) and was found at 'not counted'.

'Given from outside' against 'of the course itself' (56 uses, 39 as the marker on steps and arrows, and the basis of the headline tally at THE-MAP.md:107). It marks a real hole honestly: a premise the theorem assumes and does not derive. The word gives the hole a location, makes the course a container, and turns the missing condition into something that starts with no conditions ('something gives without waiting', 'brought in from beyond what it has'). The page's own gloss at THE-MAP.md:38 already says what is there: 'a further premise put in, which the step names'.

findings.term: reads / does not read / read by, with a law, statement, order, loop or selection as the reader

examples.quote: The law exchanging such a number reads what has stood and is insensitive at every step to every condition. Where the number differs between two sequences, the law does not read through what it is sensitive to.
That no statement reading only the represented dynamics entails the condition is a fact about the representation, in which significance is a parameter nothing else reads
"Couples into" replaced "registers", which presupposes a knower facing a world.

findings.states: Y makes a difference to X, or X depends on Y: the next step depends on these conditions; the statement's truth does not change with the order; nothing else depends on the significance parameter. Line 477 already says it this way in its own definition ("reads no order where its truth does not change with the order").
findings.note: Count: about 40 dependence uses on 29 lines by a phrase pattern (a law reads, reading no, reads only, does not read, read by ...); the whole read family (read, reads, reading, reader) is 363 occurrences on 142 lines, the chapter's most used verb. One word carries four relations here: depends on (a law reads conditions), is determined by (read off, 13), is interpreted as (read as; the label Reading [AI reading]), and is consulted or measured (a loss read by readers). The label and "read as" are an actual reader's act and are fine. The dependence sense is the finding: the chapter retired "registers" for presupposing a knower facing a world, and "reads" has the same presupposition. It is also in Lean names (ReadsNoOrder, ReadsOnlyDynamics, standing_not_read, withinCoupling_reads_iff), so a prose change would leave the identifiers.

findings.term: a selection reaches / the reach of a selection / the work's selectors

examples.quote: The selections through a selector's couplings, together, reach exactly what couples into it
coupling limits what a selection can respond to, and reading a loss, counting it and ranking courses are separate relations
for researchers in AI alignment on the theorems on what a selection reaches and the tests on trained systems

findings.note: Count: selector 7, plus selection as grammatical actor at lines 100, 115, 123, 564, 616, 743 (twice), 744, 796, 824. A noun made into a doer with a reach, facing what it does or does not reach. Swapping "reaches" for another verb keeps the doer; the sentence has to start from the coupling relation. The second half of line 100 ("are separate relations") is already said that way. "Reach" as the closure of a step relation (line 148, reach_iff_withinClosure) is a defined relation and fine.

findings.term: Optimization drains what lies beyond its couplings; "the beyond" as a noun; fed from beyond

examples.quote: T3. Optimization drains what lies beyond its couplings, where that gives room
the beyond falls by the rise and the loss (`Becoming.DrawnBeyond`)
the drain lies wherever room lies

findings.states: Take an order that rises with what couples in. At its optimum, a condition that does not couple in, and whose lower level lets the coupled ones stand higher (room), stands at its least level. "Beyond" is a relation to a named family or a named coupling closure: the conditions not in it. Line 771 nearly says this: "every optimum of any order rising with what couples in stands at the least level beyond".
findings.note: Count: drain 8; beyond 55 in all, of which 19 in prose are the place sense (lines 87, 115, 525, 545, 572 twice, 589, 602, 604 three times, 609 twice, 771 four times, 773, 819), 15 are Lean names or link slugs (fed_from_beyond, beyond_gives_nothing, rise_paid_from_beyond, loses_beyond, DrawnBeyond, grounds_beyond ...), about 20 are scope uses (beyond the model, beyond chance, beyond relations) that are fine, and one is the denial at line 92. "Outside" is 23, mostly module scope or denials ("a law standing outside what it holds of", line 633), which are fine. A doer (optimization), a done-to (what is drained) and a place (the beyond). The theorems themselves always name the family or closure, so the basis exists; the thesis title and the bare noun drop it.

findings.term: own / self-concern / de se / center / standpoint

examples.quote: What is open is which relation, or which class, is a center's own, which is the step of invariance
Call a life's order over courses *self-concerned* when it ranks above what it widens every widening that adds to its own continuation, read as what lies within its reach.
The step is reduced to whether the self's presupposition in acting is essentially de se and whether a relation privileges the self's drawing

findings.states: "Own" is the closure of one line along a chosen relation: everything that can, at some remove, make a difference to its going on. Which relation and which class is not derived; it is a supplied parameter (line 254, "standpoints and their own regions") and an open item (12).
findings.note: Count: self-concern 41, de se 21, standpoint 17; "own" alone is 95 by grep but that includes idiom (its own receipts) and Lean names, so the self sense is an estimate of about 40 more. The chapter says the hole openly, so this is a slot kept honest, not a name to replace: a new word for self-concern would hide that the self/other line is taken, not shown.
